lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: A Visit to the Park
lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short

One bright sunny morning, Hamza and Abdullah go to their neighbourhood park. It is Sunday and both friends are in high spirits. They stop outside the park to buy some ice cream from a small shop near the gate.

  • Hamza wants to throw his ice cream wrapper on the ground.
  • Abdullah stops him and says we should keep Pakistan clean and beautiful.
  • They read the park rules written on a big board at the park gate.
  • They decide to put up posters and place dustbins with signs of 'Keep Pakistan Clean' on them.

Word Meanings

  • trash — garbage
  • heap — pile
  • high spirits — lively and cheerful behaviour or mood
  • chatting — talking
  • wrapper — a piece of paper or plastic that covers something, like a sweet or a packet of biscuit
  • realize — understand or know something

City Park Rules

  • You must not write or draw on the walls of the park.
  • You must not throw trash around the park. Use the provided dustbins.
  • You must not cut or harm the plants and trees.
  • You must not write on or damage the benches.
  • You must follow the park timings: from 8:00 am to 8:00 pm daily.
  • Children must come with an adult.

Key Points

The most suitable title for this text is 'Keeping Public Places Clean'. Public places are for all of us to use. If we do not take care of them, we will have no place left for fun and enjoyment.

mcqs.q: On which day did Hamza and Abdullah go to the park?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sunday. The text begins: 'One bright sunny morning, Hamza and Abdullah decide to go to their neighbourhood park. It is Sunday and both friends are in high spirits.' So the story happens on a Sunday morning.

mcqs.q: How was the morning when the two friends went to the park?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is bright and sunny. The first line of the text says, 'One bright sunny morning.' That is why the book's true/false statement 'They set out on a rainy day' is false.

mcqs.q: What did the friends buy from the small shop near the gate?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ice cream. The text says they stopped outside the park to buy some ice cream from a small shop near the gate. The whole lesson grows out of what Hamza wants to do with the ice cream wrapper.

mcqs.q: What did Abdullah tell Hamza not to do?
options: Not to talk in the park
Not to throw his ice cream wrapper on the ground
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: not to throw his ice cream wrapper on the ground. Abdullah says, 'You should not throw your ice cream wrapper on the ground, Hamza!' He wants Hamza to use a dustbin instead.

mcqs.q: Why did Hamza want to throw the wrapper on the ground?
options: Because everyone else throws trash around there
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because everyone else throws trash around there. Hamza says, 'Why shouldn't I? Everyone else throws trash around here.' Abdullah teaches him that if everyone throws single pieces of trash, it will soon create a rubbish heap.

mcqs.q: What is the most suitable title for this text?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Keeping Public Places Clean'. The whole text is about following park rules and keeping public places clean. The other titles name only small parts of the story, not its main idea.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'trash' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is garbage. In the vocabulary exercise, 'trash' is matched with 'garbage'. Abdullah says that if we all throw single pieces of trash it will create a rubbish heap in the park.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'wrapper' mean?
options: A piece of paper or plastic that covers something
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a piece of paper or plastic that covers something, like a sweet or a packet of biscuit. Hamza's ice cream wrapper is the piece of paper he was about to throw on the ground.

mcqs.q: Where was the board on which the park rules were written?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: at the park gate. Abdullah takes Hamza back to the park gate, where there is a huge board that reads 'Park Rules'. Hamza says he never noticed it before.

mcqs.q: What are the park timings?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8:00 am to 8:00 pm. Rule 5 on the board says: 'You must follow the park timings: from 8:00 am to 8:00 pm daily.' That is why the statement giving 7:30 am is false.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT allowed in the park?
options: Writing on the walls and benches
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: writing on the walls and benches. The park rules clearly say, 'You must not write or draw on the walls of the park' and 'You must not write on/damage the benches.' The other three things are allowed or required.

mcqs.q: Children must come to the park ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: with an adult. Rule 6 of the City Park Rules says, 'Children must come with an adult.' This rule keeps children safe in the park.

mcqs.q: What two things did Abdullah and Hamza decide to do to teach people about keeping the park clean?
options: Write on the walls and benches
Close the park and lock the gate
Put up posters and place dustbins with 'Keep Pakistan Clean' signs
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: put up posters and place dustbins with 'Keep Pakistan Clean' signs. Hamza says just putting up rules is not enough; we should teach others how to keep public places clean.

mcqs.q: Why should we take care of public places?
options: Because the park is our own house
Because the watchman tells us to
Because public places are for all of us to use; if we do not take care of them, no place will be left for fun and enjoyment
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because public places are for all of us to use. Abdullah says, 'If we do not take care of them, we will have no place left for fun and enjoyment.' Parks, schools, hospitals and libraries belong to everyone.

mcqs.q: The signs the two friends would put up would say ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Keep Pakistan Clean'. The friends decide to place dustbins all around the park with signs of 'Keep Pakistan Clean' on them, so that everyone learns to keep the country clean.

lessons.title: Speaking: Seek and Respond
lessons.notes_html:
What We Learn

In this section we practise a conversation about road safety. One student plays the role of Amina and the other plays Sadia. Then we change roles and repeat the dialogue.

The Dialogue — Key Lines

  • Amina: Look at me! See how fast I can run on the main road.
  • Sadia: You must not run on the main road! It's against the law.
  • Sadia: You must walk on the side where you can see the traffic coming.
  • Sadia: You must follow these rules for your safety.
  • Amina: Yes, I know. I must obey the rules. Thank you, Sadia.

Key Points

We use must and must not to talk about rules. Running on the main road is against the law and dangerous. We must follow traffic rules for our safety. After practising, we can change the activity, for example: walk alone in the dark, or walk on a train track, and make new dialogues.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, what does Amina want to do?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: run on the main road. Amina says, 'Look at me! See how fast I can run on the main road.' Sadia stops her because this is dangerous and against the law.

mcqs.q: What does Sadia say to Amina?
options: You may run on the main road
You must not run on the main road
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'You must not run on the main road!' Sadia uses 'must not' because running on the main road is a rule of safety and it is against the law.

mcqs.q: Running on the main road is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: against the law. Sadia says, 'You must not run on the main road! It's against the law.' Laws are rules made for everyone's safety.

mcqs.q: Where must we walk, according to Sadia?
options: In the middle of the road
On the side where we can see the traffic coming
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: on the side where we can see the traffic coming. Sadia says, 'You must walk on the side where you can see the traffic coming.' Then we can see vehicles and keep safe.

mcqs.q: Why must we follow these rules?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: for our safety. Sadia says, 'You must follow these rules for your safety.' Traffic rules protect us from accidents on the road.

mcqs.q: The words 'must not' show that something is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: not allowed. We use 'must not' for prohibition — when a thing is against the rules or the law, like running on the main road or throwing trash in the park.

mcqs.q: What does Amina say at the end of the dialogue?
options: I will run on the road again
Yes, I know. I must obey the rules
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Yes, I know. I must obey the rules.' Amina understands Sadia's words and thanks her. She learns that rules are for her own safety.

mcqs.q: Who stops Amina from running on the main road?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sadia. In the pair dialogue, Sadia plays the role of the careful friend who explains the rules: you must not run on the main road, and you must walk where you can see the traffic coming.

mcqs.q: After practising the dialogue, students change roles and then change the activity. Which is an example of a new activity from the book?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: walk alone in the dark. The book says that after practising, students can change the activity, e.g. walk alone in the dark, walk on a train track, etc., and use must/must not for the new rules.

mcqs.q: In pair practice, after one student plays Amina and the other plays Sadia, what do they do next?
options: Change roles and repeat the dialogue
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: change roles and repeat the dialogue. The book instructs: first one student plays Amina and the other Sadia, then change roles and repeat, so both students practise every line.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Must, Must Not, Should, Should Not
lessons.notes_html:
Should / Should Not — For Advice

We use should and should not to give advice — to tell someone what is good or bad to do.

  • You should not throw your ice cream wrapper on the ground, Hamza!
  • If we want a clean and beautiful Pakistan, we should try and make it one.
  • You should use it (this public park) wisely!
  • We should teach others how to keep the public places clean.
  • Advice example: You should treat animals kindly.

Must / Must Not — For Rules

We use must and must not for strong rules, duties and things that are not allowed.

  • We must follow the park rules here and protect our public places.
  • You must not write or draw on the walls of the park.
  • You must not throw trash around the park.
  • You must not cut or harm the plants and trees.
  • You must follow the park timings.
  • Children must come with an adult.
  • Rule example: You must not shout in class.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words do we use to give advice?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is should / should not. The book says we use 'should' and 'should not' for advice, like 'You should treat animals kindly.' Must and must not are used for strong rules.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words shows a strong rule or something not allowed?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is must / must not. The park rules use 'must not': 'You must not write or draw on the walls of the park.' Must not shows prohibition — a thing is not allowed at all.

mcqs.q: Complete the park rule: 'You ______ not write or draw on the walls of the park.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'must'. This is Rule 1 on the City Park board: 'You must not write or draw on the walls of the park.' It is a strict rule, not just advice, so we use must not.

mcqs.q: Complete Abdullah's sentence: 'If we want a clean and beautiful Pakistan, we ______ try and make it one.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'should'. Abdullah gives advice here: 'we should try and make it one.' He is telling Hamza what is the right and good thing to do.

mcqs.q: Complete the park rule: 'Children ______ come with an adult.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'must'. Rule 6 on the board says, 'Children must come with an adult.' It is a duty for safety, so the strong word 'must' is used.

mcqs.q: 'You should treat animals kindly.' This sentence is an example of ______.
options: an order from the park board
mcqs.why: The correct answer is advice. In the group activity, the book gives this sentence as an example of advice for the ADVICE page. Advice tells us what is good to do, and it uses 'should'.

mcqs.q: 'You must not shout in class.' This sentence is an example of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a rule. The book gives this sentence as an example for the RULES page. Rules use 'must' and 'must not' because they must be obeyed.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a rule from the City Park board?
options: You should try and make Pakistan beautiful
We should teach others to keep places clean
You must follow the park timings
You should use the park wisely
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'You must follow the park timings.' This is Rule 5 written on the park board. The other sentences are advice that Abdullah gives in the story, using 'should'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'We ______ teach others how to keep the public places clean.' (Abdullah's advice)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'should'. This line is in the should/should not column of the book's table. Teaching others is good advice for everyone, so Abdullah uses 'should'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'We ______ follow the park rules here and protect our public places.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'must'. Abdullah says, 'Therefore, we must follow the park rules here and protect our public places.' Following rules is a duty, so 'must' is used.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Present Continuous Tense
lessons.notes_html:
Present Continuous Tense

We use the Present Continuous Tense to talk about actions that are happening now, at this time.

Form: am / is / are + verb-ing

  • I am decorating the classroom.
  • He / She is playing.
  • We / They are enjoying themselves.

Examples from the Book — In the Park

  • Saba is swinging on the swing.
  • Asad is sliding down the slide.
  • Beena, John, Kumar and Sita are playing on the see-saw.
  • Rafiq is kicking a football.
  • Rani is skipping with a rope.
  • Zahid is running around the park.

Examples — Eid Milan Party in the Classroom

  • Ayesha is decorating the classroom with balloons.
  • Ali is arranging the chairs in a circle.
  • Ahmed is bringing cold drinks.
  • Our teacher is helping us and smiling.

We begin such a paragraph with a topic sentence like 'All the children are enjoying themselves in the park' and end it with a concluding sentence like 'In short, all of them are having a good time.'

mcqs.q: The Present Continuous Tense is used for actions that are ______.
options: done every day in the past
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: happening now. In this lesson we describe what children are doing in the park at this time: 'Saba is swinging', 'Rafiq is kicking a football.' The action is going on as we speak.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Saba ______ swinging on the swing.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'is'. Saba is one person (she), so we use 'is' with the -ing form: 'Saba is swinging on the swing.' With I we use 'am', and with we/they we use 'are'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Asad is ______ down the slide.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'sliding'. In the Present Continuous we add -ing to the verb: is + sliding. The book's model paragraph says, 'Asad is sliding down the slide.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Beena, John, Kumar and Sita ______ playing on the see-saw.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'are'. Beena, John, Kumar and Sita are four children — a plural subject like 'they' — so we use 'are playing'. For one person we would use 'is playing'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Rafiq is ______ a football.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'kicking'. The present continuous form is is + verb-ing: 'Rafiq is kicking a football.' All the sentences in this paragraph describe actions happening in the park right now.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Rani is skipping with a ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'rope'. The book's model paragraph says, 'Rani is skipping with a rope.' Skipping is done with a rope, and Rani is doing it in the park.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is in the Present Continuous Tense?
options: Our teacher will help us tomorrow
Our teacher is helping us and smiling
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Our teacher is helping us and smiling.' It has is + verb-ing, which shows an action happening now. The other sentences are past, future or daily-habit sentences.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'I ______ decorating the classroom with balloons.' (Ayesha)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'am'. With 'I' we always use 'am' in the Present Continuous: 'I am decorating...' In the book's Eid Milan model, 'Ayesha is decorating the classroom with balloons.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Ali is ______ the chairs in a circle.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'arranging'. The sentence is about the Eid Milan party preparations happening now, so we use is + arranging: 'Ali is arranging the chairs in a circle.'

mcqs.q: Which is a good concluding sentence for the park paragraph?
options: Saba is swinging on the swing
Zahid is running around the park
In short, all of them are having a good time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'In short, all of them are having a good time.' The book teaches us to end the paragraph with a concluding sentence beginning with a phrase like 'In short'. The other sentences are detail sentences from the middle of the paragraph.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Cohesive Devices and Punctuation
lessons.notes_html:
Cohesive Devices — Ending a Paragraph

The phrases in brief, in short and to sum up join the ideas of a paragraph together. We use them at the beginning of the last (concluding) sentence of a paragraph, and we use each phrase only once.

  • In short, we are all responsible for taking care of our parks.
  • In brief, we should complete our homework on time in order to be good students.
  • To sum up, we must respect our parents and be kind to them.

Remember: put a comma after the phrase. A paragraph begins with a topic sentence that tells what the paragraph is about.

Punctuation — Quotation Marks

We use quotation marks (" ") to enclose a direct quotation — the exact words of a speaker. A comma comes before the quotation, and the first word inside the marks begins with a capital letter.

  • Father said to me, "Finish your work!"
  • Kamran said, "Mehnaz wants to play outside."
  • "Which shop do you want to go to?" asked mother.
  • "I'm next," she said softly.
  • Nyla told me, "You are the best!"

In the story of the blind young man, all the spoken words are written with quotation marks, commas and capital letters in the same way.

mcqs.q: The phrases 'in brief', 'in short' and 'to sum up' are used ______.
options: at the beginning of the last sentence of a paragraph
at the start of the first sentence
in the title of the paragraph
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: at the beginning of the last sentence of a paragraph. The book says: add 'in brief', 'in short' or 'to sum up' at the beginning of the last sentence. That last sentence concludes the whole paragraph.

mcqs.q: After writing 'In brief' at the start of the concluding sentence, we put a ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a comma. The book reminds us: 'remember to use a comma after it.' For example: 'In brief, we should complete our homework on time.'

mcqs.q: In one exercise with three paragraphs, each phrase (in brief / in short / to sum up) should be used ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: only once. The instruction says, 'Use each phrase only once.' So the three paragraphs end with three different phrases, one in each paragraph.

mcqs.q: Quotation marks are used to enclose ______.
options: a direct quotation — the exact words of a speaker
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a direct quotation. This unit's language focus is 'Use quotation marks to enclose a direct quotation', for example: Father said to me, "Finish your work!"

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Father said to me finish your work!
"Father said to me finish your work!"
father said to me, finish your work!
Father said to me, "Finish your work!"
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Father said to me, "Finish your work!" This is the book's own worked example: a comma after 'me', quotation marks around the spoken words, and a capital F for 'Finish'.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Kamran said Mehnaz wants to play outside.
Kamran said "Mehnaz wants to play outside"
kamran said, "mehnaz wants to play outside."
Kamran said, "Mehnaz wants to play outside."
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Kamran said, "Mehnaz wants to play outside." We need a comma after 'said' and quotation marks around Mehnaz's words, with a capital M at the start of the quotation.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Which shop do you want to go to? asked mother.
Which shop do you want to go to, asked mother?
"Which shop do you want to go to?" asked mother.
"which shop do you want to go to"? asked mother.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: "Which shop do you want to go to?" asked mother. When the spoken words come first, the whole question stays inside the quotation marks, including the question mark.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: "I'm next," she said softly. The comma goes inside the quotation marks at the end of the spoken words, before 'she said softly'.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Nyla told me you are the best!
"Nyla told me you are the best!"
Nyla told me, you are the best!
Nyla told me, "You are the best!"
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Nyla told me, "You are the best!" The exact words of Nyla are inside quotation marks, and the exclamation mark stays inside the marks too.

mcqs.q: The first sentence of a paragraph, which tells what the paragraph is about, is called the ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: topic sentence. In the writing exercise on 'your school', the book says: first do brainstorming, then write a good topic sentence, then write the points in detail, and finally end with a concluding sentence.

lessons.title: Writing: Dialogues
lessons.notes_html:
Writing a Dialogue-Story

Topic: Keeping Our Village/City Clean. Work in groups of three and follow these steps:

  • Discuss how you can keep your village/city clean.
  • Draw a mind map and note down all the main points on its lines.
  • Discuss what your story will be, what the scene will be, how many characters you will have and what their names will be.
  • Write down the dialogues. Use should/should not for advice and must/must not for rules.
  • Give a title to your story and write the complete dialogue-story in your notebook.

Model Dialogue — Keeping Our City Clean

  • Ali: Look at this street! There is trash everywhere.
  • Sara: Yes, it looks so dirty. We should keep our city clean.
  • Bilal: You are right. We must not throw trash on the roads.
  • Ali: We should use the dustbins. We should also tell others to keep the city clean.
  • Sara: We must follow the rules. We must not throw wrappers on the ground.
  • Bilal: Let us put up posters that say 'Keep Our City Clean'.
  • Ali: Great idea! If we all work together, our city will become clean and beautiful.

mcqs.q: What is the topic of the dialogue-story in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Keeping Our Village/City Clean. The writing section asks groups to discuss this topic, draw a mind map, and then turn their ideas into a dialogue-story like the reading text of Unit 1.

mcqs.q: Before writing the dialogues, students draw a ______ and note down the main points on its lines.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a mind map. The steps say: 'in your notebooks draw a mind map like this; note down all the main points on the lines in the mind map.' A mind map collects all our ideas before we write.

mcqs.q: In a dialogue, we use should / should not for ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is advice. The book's step says: 'remember to use should/should not for advice and must/must not for rules.' For example, Sara says, 'We should keep our city clean.'

mcqs.q: In a dialogue, we use must / must not for ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is rules. For example, Bilal says, 'We must not throw trash on the roads,' and Sara says, 'We must follow the rules.' Rules are strong and must be obeyed.

mcqs.q: Every dialogue-story must have a ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a title. One of the steps is: 'give a title to your story.' The model dialogue's title is 'Keeping Our City Clean'.

mcqs.q: In the model dialogue, who says, 'Look at this street! There is trash everywhere'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ali. Ali speaks the first line of the model dialogue and points out the trash on the street. Then Sara and Bilal give their ideas about keeping the city clean.

mcqs.q: Complete Sara's line: 'We ______ keep our city clean.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'should'. Sara's line is advice: 'We should keep our city clean.' Advice about good actions uses should, while strict rules use must.

mcqs.q: Complete Bilal's line: 'We ______ not throw trash on the roads.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'must'. Bilal's full line is: 'You are right. We must not throw trash on the roads.' Throwing trash is against the cleanliness rules, so 'must not' is used.

mcqs.q: What do the friends in the model dialogue decide to put up?
options: Posters that say 'Keep Our City Clean'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: posters that say 'Keep Our City Clean'. Bilal says, 'Let us put up posters that say Keep Our City Clean.' Posters teach many people at one time.

mcqs.q: How many students work together in one group for this writing activity?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The book says, 'Work in groups of three and follow these steps.' Three students discuss the points, make the mind map and write the dialogues together.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Self-Created Cloze
lessons.notes_html:
Self-Created Cloze

Do you want to speak and write good English? Doing this activity every day can help you. You can use your English textbook or any other book in English, and you will need an extra notebook.

Steps

  • 1. Choose a paragraph from the Reading Comprehension section of your English textbook or any other book in English.
  • 2. Mark or underline every 8th word.
  • 3. Open your notebook. Draw a margin and put the date.
  • 4. Copy the paragraph in your best handwriting in your notebook.
  • 5. Do not write the marked/underlined word. Draw a blank line where the word is.
  • 6. Close the books. Take a break of half an hour.
  • 7. Take out your notebook and fill in the blanks without looking at the original paragraph.

Check Your Work

  • Have you put in a margin? Have you put in the date?
  • Have you started the paragraph two-finger space away from the margin?
  • Does the writing look neat and tidy?
  • Open your textbook and check your answers in the blanks. Give yourself one mark for each correct answer.

Try to write at least one paragraph every day. Do this activity even when you go to Class VII and VIII.

mcqs.q: In the Self-Created Cloze activity, which word do we mark or underline?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: every 8th word. Step 2 of the activity says, 'Mark or underline every 8th word.' Later we leave a blank in place of each marked word and try to fill it from memory.

mcqs.q: Where do we copy the paragraph for this activity?
options: In an extra notebook, in our best handwriting
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in an extra notebook, in our best handwriting. The book says we need an extra notebook for this activity, and step 4 says to copy the paragraph in your best handwriting.

mcqs.q: What do we draw in place of the marked word?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a blank line. Step 5 says: 'Do not write the marked/underlined word. Draw a blank line where the word is.' The word 'cloze' activity is all about filling these blanks later.

mcqs.q: After copying the paragraph, how long a break do we take?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: half an hour. Step 6 says, 'Close the books. Take a break of half an hour.' The break makes us fill the blanks from our own memory, not by copying.

mcqs.q: When we fill in the blanks, we should fill them ______.
options: without looking at the original paragraph
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: without looking at the original paragraph. Step 7 says to take out the notebook and fill in the blanks without looking. Only after that do we open the textbook to check.

mcqs.q: How many marks do we give ourselves for each correct answer?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one mark. The checking step says: 'Give yourself one mark for each correct answer.' This is how we score our own cloze work.

mcqs.q: The paragraph in our notebook should start ______ away from the margin.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: two-finger space. The check list asks: 'Have you started the paragraph two-finger space away from the margin?' This keeps our writing neat and tidy.

mcqs.q: From where can we choose a paragraph for the Self-Created Cloze?
options: From the Reading Comprehension section of the English textbook or any other book in English
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: from the Reading Comprehension section of the English textbook or any other book in English. Step 1 gives both choices, so we can practise with new paragraphs every day.

mcqs.q: How often should we do the Self-Created Cloze activity?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: every day. The book says, 'Try to write at least one paragraph every day,' and to keep doing this activity even in Class VII and VIII. Daily practice makes our English strong.

mcqs.q: What two things must we put at the top of the notebook page before copying?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a margin and the date. Step 3 says, 'Open your notebook. Draw a margin and put the date.' The check list also asks: 'Have you put in a margin? Have you put in the date?'

lessons.title: Fun: Making Colourful Posters
lessons.notes_html:
Making Colourful Posters

Work in groups of three and make colourful posters on any one of the following topics:

  • 1. Keeping our park clean
  • 2. Keeping our village/city clean
  • 3. Keeping our school clean
  • 4. Keeping our house clean
  • 5. Keeping the area around our house clean

After Making the Poster

  • Take turns during assembly to show your posters and give information about them.
  • Present your posters in front of another class.
  • Put them on display around your school.

A Good Poster

A good poster has a big, clear title and colourful pictures. For example, a poster on 'Keeping Our Park Clean' can show a clean park with green trees, dustbins and children playing, with messages like 'Keep Our Park Clean' and 'Use the Dustbins' written on it. In this way posters teach people how and why to keep places clean — the same idea Hamza had in the reading text.

mcqs.q: How many students make a poster together in one group?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The Fun section says, 'Work in groups of three and make colourful posters.' Group work lets students share drawing, writing and presenting.

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of the poster topics in the book?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Keeping our school clean. The five topics in the book are: park, village/city, school, house, and the area around our house. The other options are not in the book's list.

mcqs.q: Where do students first show their posters and give information about them?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: during assembly. The book says, 'Take turns during assembly to show your posters and give information about them.' In this way the whole school learns the cleanliness message.

mcqs.q: After the assembly, the posters are also presented ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in front of another class. The book's second step after completing the poster is: 'Present your posters in front of another class.' Then the posters are displayed around the school.

mcqs.q: Where are the finished posters put on display?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: around the school. The book says, 'Put them on display around your school.' Everyone who passes by reads the cleanliness messages again and again.

mcqs.q: Which of these topics is NOT in the book's poster list?
options: Keeping the area around our house clean
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Keeping our hospital clean. The book lists five topics: park, village/city, school, house, and the area around our house. Hospital is not among them.

mcqs.q: Posters about cleanliness teach people ______.
options: how and why to keep places clean
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: how and why to keep places clean. This was Hamza's idea in the reading text: 'We can put up posters telling people how and why to keep the places clean.'

mcqs.q: A model poster on 'Keeping Our Park Clean' should show ______.
options: a clean park with green trees, dustbins and children playing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a clean park with green trees, dustbins and children playing. The solved answer describes such a poster with the messages 'Keep Our Park Clean' and 'Use the Dustbins' written on it.

mcqs.q: The message 'Use the Dustbins' tells people to ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: throw trash in the dustbins. This is also a City Park rule: 'You must not throw trash around the park. Use the provided dustbins.' Posters remind people of this rule.

mcqs.q: This Fun activity is connected with the reading text because ______.
options: Hamza also decided to put up posters to teach people
the park has many posters already
posters are sold in the park
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Hamza also decided to put up posters to teach people. In 'A Visit to the Park', Hamza says that just putting up rules is not enough — we should teach others with posters. The Fun activity lets us do the same thing.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: A Dream that Brought a Big Change
lessons.notes_html:
The Story in Short

Kamal dreams that he is standing at the railway station while all his classmates get on the train to go to Lahore, Islamabad and Murree. He is crying because the school doctor has said that Kamal is weak and unhealthy, so he cannot go with them.

  • The doctor says Kamal has a bad cough and sometimes fever, and he cannot walk long distances or climb hills.
  • His friends Yousuf and Ejaz are also not healthy, so they also cannot go.
  • The doctor advises Kamal: take proper food, do physical exercise, sleep early and wake up early, do not eat too many sweets, paan or chhaliya, eat fruits and vegetables, take a bath daily, and wash hands before every meal.
  • Kamal wakes up. His mother is shaking him. It was all a dream!
  • After the dream Kamal decides to change his life: he will eat proper food, stay clean, play outside and go to bed early.

Characters in the Story

There are four main characters: Kamal, the doctor, Kamal's mother and Kamal's classmates (including Yousuf and Ejaz). Kamal is present both in the dream and after the dream. His mother comes only after he wakes up.

Key Points

  • The last thing Kamal said in his dream was: 'Please let me go to Murree. I will do what you tell me. Please, please, please.'
  • The dream brought a big change in Kamal's life.
  • Opposite words from the text: laughing–crying, weak–strong, unhealthy–healthy, always–never, clean–dirty, active–inactive.

mcqs.q: Where was Kamal standing in his dream?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: at the railway station. The story opens: 'Kamal was standing at the railway station. All his classmates were getting on the train.' He waved at them but he was crying.

mcqs.q: Why could Kamal not go to Lahore, Islamabad and Murree with his classmates?
options: The doctor said he was weak and unhealthy
His mother did not allow him
He had no money for the ticket
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the doctor said he was weak and unhealthy. The school doctor said Kamal 'should not be allowed to go' because he could not walk long distances and climb hills.

mcqs.q: What health problems did the doctor name for Kamal?
options: A bad cough and sometimes fever
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a bad cough and sometimes fever. The doctor says, 'Besides, you have a bad cough and sometimes you have fever. How can you walk long distances and carry your bags when you are not well?'

mcqs.q: Which of Kamal's friends were also not healthy?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Yousuf and Ejaz. The doctor tells Kamal, 'Your friends, Yousuf and Ejaz, are also not healthy. They will also not be allowed to go.'

mcqs.q: Which food did the doctor tell Kamal to eat MORE of?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: fruits and vegetables. The doctor says, 'Instead, you should eat fruits and vegetables.' He also tells Kamal to wash the fruits and vegetables before eating them.

mcqs.q: Which things did the doctor tell Kamal NOT to eat too many of?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: sweets, paan and chhaliya. The doctor says, 'You should not eat too many sweets, or paan, or chhaliya.' These things make us sick and unhealthy.

mcqs.q: When should Kamal sleep and wake up, according to the doctor?
options: Sleep late and wake up late
Sleep late and wake up early
Sleep early and wake up early
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: sleep early and wake up early. This is one of the doctor's pieces of advice. After waking, Kamal also promises his mother that he will not watch too much television but will go to bed early.

mcqs.q: When should Kamal wash his hands?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: before every meal. The doctor says, 'You should also take a bath daily and wash your hands before every meal.' Clean hands keep germs away from our food.

mcqs.q: Who woke Kamal up from his dream?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: his mother. She was shaking him and said, 'Kamal. Wake up. Why are you crying? Did you have a bad dream?' Kamal's mother is not in the dream; she comes after he wakes up.

mcqs.q: What was the last thing Kamal said in his dream?
options: 'Please let me go to Murree. I will do what you tell me. Please, please, please.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Please let me go to Murree. I will do what you tell me. Please, please, please.' After saying this, Kamal woke up and found his mother shaking him.

mcqs.q: Which character is present both in the dream and after the dream?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Kamal. The story is Kamal's own dream, so he is in the dream, and he is also there after waking up. The doctor and classmates are only in the dream, and his mother comes only after the dream.

mcqs.q: What change did the dream bring in Kamal?
options: He decided to eat proper food, exercise, sleep early and wake up early
He decided never to go to school
He decided to eat more sweets
He decided to watch more television
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: he decided to eat proper food, exercise, sleep early and wake up early. Kamal tells his mother he will have milk, fish, meat, vegetables and fruits, play outside after homework, and go to bed early. That is why the title is 'A Dream that Brought a Big Change'.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of the word 'weak' in the text?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'strong'. In the vocabulary exercise, List 1 words are matched with their opposites in List 2: weak–strong, unhealthy–healthy, laughing–crying, clean–dirty, always–never.

mcqs.q: Kamal said, 'But, I always walk to school.' This was said ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in his dream. In the book's exercise, this statement is marked 'In His Dream' as the example. Kamal says it to the doctor while arguing that he is not weak.

mcqs.q: Why did Kamal say he would take a bath every day before going to bed?
options: Because if we remain clean we will not fall sick
Because the doctor will check him
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because if we remain clean we will not fall sick. Kamal matches this reason with the statement himself in the exercise: cleanliness protects us from sickness.

lessons.title: Speaking: Showing Willingness and Unwillingness
lessons.notes_html:
What We Learn

In this section we show willingness (I will...) and unwillingness (I will not...) to do something. One student plays Zohra and the other plays Razia. Then we change roles and repeat the dialogue.

The Dialogue — Key Lines

  • Zohra: Will you come to my house on Sunday?
  • Razia: No, I will go to my uncle's house.
  • Zohra: Will you do some work there?
  • Razia: Yes, I will do some work but mostly I will play with my cousins.
  • Zohra: Will you watch TV?
  • Razia: No, I will not watch TV. I can watch TV at home.
  • Razia: We will mostly play outdoor games; like cricket, skipping, racing, etc.

Key Points

Questions about the future begin with Will you...? We answer with 'Yes, I will' or 'No, I will not'. After practising, we can change the activity, for example: 'help me do my homework' or 'will you take part in the annual sports'.

mcqs.q: Where will Razia go on Sunday?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to her uncle's house. When Zohra asks, 'Will you come to my house on Sunday?' Razia answers, 'No, I will go to my uncle's house.' This shows unwillingness to come and willingness to go somewhere else.

mcqs.q: What will Razia mostly do at her uncle's house?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: play with her cousins. Razia says, 'Yes, I will do some work but mostly I will play with my cousins.' She will do some work too, but playing is the main activity.

mcqs.q: Will Razia watch TV at her uncle's house?
options: No, she will not watch TV because she can watch TV at home
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: No, she will not watch TV. Razia says, 'No, I will not watch TV. I can watch TV at home.' This is an example of showing unwillingness — 'I will not'.

mcqs.q: Which games will Razia and her cousins mostly play?
options: Outdoor games like cricket, skipping and racing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: outdoor games like cricket, skipping and racing. Razia says, 'We will mostly play outdoor games; like cricket, skipping, racing, etc.' Outdoor games are good for health, which is the theme of this unit.

mcqs.q: Which question asks about willingness in the future?
options: Will you come to my house on Sunday?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Will you come to my house on Sunday?' Questions for this speaking skill begin with 'Will you...?' The answer 'I will' shows willingness and 'I will not' shows unwillingness.

mcqs.q: 'No, I will not watch TV' shows ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is unwillingness. The title of this section is 'Showing Willingness and Unwillingness to do Something'. 'I will not' clearly shows that the speaker does not want to do the thing.

mcqs.q: What does Zohra say at the end of the dialogue?
options: Have a good weekend. Enjoy yourself
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Have a good weekend. Enjoy yourself.' Zohra wishes Razia well, and Razia replies, 'I will. Thank you.' This is a polite way to end a conversation.

mcqs.q: After practising the Zohra–Razia dialogue, students ______.
options: change roles and repeat the dialogue
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: change roles and repeat the dialogue. The book says: first one student plays Zohra and the other Razia, then change roles and repeat, so both students practise asking and answering.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of a new activity the book suggests for more practice?
options: 'Help me do my homework' / 'Will you take part in the annual sports?'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'help me do my homework' and 'will you take part in the annual sports'. The solved answer says students can then change the activity, e.g. help me do my homework, will you take part in the annual sports, etc.

mcqs.q: Razia will do some work at her uncle's house. This shows ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is willingness. Razia says, 'Yes, I will do some work.' 'Yes, I will' is the short way of showing willingness to do something in the future.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Pronouns as Reference Words
lessons.notes_html:
Reflexive Pronouns

Reflexive pronouns end in -self or -selves. We use them when the doer and the receiver of the action are the same.

  • I — myself: I did it myself.
  • You (one person) — yourself: You must polish your shoes yourself.
  • He — himself: Ahmad likes talking to himself.
  • She — herself: Ayesha washed her sock herself.
  • It — itself: The car moved by itself.
  • We — ourselves: Fatima, Alia and I cleaned it ourselves.
  • You (many people) — yourselves: You must complete the work yourselves.
  • They — themselves: Mustafa and Abbas hurt themselves.

Pronouns as Reference Words

A pronoun stands in place of a noun and refers to it.

  • Aslam is a nice boy. He helps everyone. (He — Aslam)
  • The soldiers are very brave. They always protect our country. (They — the soldiers)
  • The train came at 6 o'clock. It was on time. (It — the train)
  • My mother was not at home. She had gone to buy some milk. (She — my mother)
  • The dog was barking loudly. It had seen a stranger near the door. (It — the dog)

mcqs.q: Complete: 'I did it ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'myself'. With 'I', the reflexive pronoun is 'myself'. The book's matching exercise gives: 'I did it myself.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Ahmad likes talking to ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'himself'. Ahmad is a boy (he), so the reflexive pronoun is 'himself': 'Ahmad likes talking to himself.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Mustafa and Abbas hurt ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'themselves'. Mustafa and Abbas are two people (they), so we use the plural reflexive pronoun 'themselves': 'Mustafa and Abbas hurt themselves.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'The car moved by ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'itself'. A car is a thing (it), so its reflexive pronoun is 'itself': 'The car moved by itself.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Fatima, Alia and I cleaned it ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'ourselves'. 'Fatima, Alia and I' means 'we', and the reflexive pronoun for 'we' is 'ourselves'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Be careful with that knife. You might cut ______.' (one person)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'yourself'. The book marks this blank '(singular)' — one person — so we use 'yourself'. For two or more people we would use 'yourselves'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Would you two like to get ______ some milk?' (two people)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'yourselves'. The book marks this blank '(plural)' because it talks to two people ('you two'). Plural 'you' takes 'yourselves'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'The bird was making a nest by ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'itself'. A bird is referred to as 'it' in this exercise, so the reflexive pronoun is 'itself': 'The bird was making a nest by itself.'

mcqs.q: 'The train came at 6 o'clock. It was on time.' The pronoun 'It' refers to ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the train. Pronouns are reference words — they point back to a noun. Here 'It' stands for 'the train' in the first sentence.

mcqs.q: 'My mother was not at home. She had gone to buy some milk.' The pronoun 'She' refers to ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: my mother. In the book's table, sentence 5 'She' refers to 'My mother'. Reading the sentence before tells us who the pronoun stands for.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Past Continuous Tense and Punctuation
lessons.notes_html:
Past Continuous Tense

We use the Past Continuous Tense to talk about actions that were going on at a past time.

Form: was / were + verb-ing

  • My father was reading the newspaper at 7 o'clock in the morning.
  • My mother was cooking lunch when I was in school.
  • I was playing with my friends at 5 o'clock in the evening.
  • My mother was sleeping at 11 o'clock at night.

Story Example — The Bird and the Ant

'One day a bird was sitting on a tree near a stream. It was looking down at the water below. Suddenly it saw that an ant was sinking in the water. It was trying to get out but the water was flowing very fast.' Later the ant saves the bird from a hunter in the same way.

Punctuation — Capital Letters and Full Stops

Every sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. Names of people and places also begin with capital letters.

  • I often go for long walks on summer evenings. It is peaceful and I can exercise too.
  • At the Eid fair last Saturday Ali saw a clown. He was wearing a red coat.
  • Imdad and Salim are in class 6. Last Friday they had a fight in class.

mcqs.q: The Past Continuous Tense is formed with ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: was/were + verb-ing. For example, 'My father was reading the newspaper at 7 o'clock.' We use 'was' with I/he/she/it and 'were' with we/you/they.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'My mother ______ lunch when I was in school.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'was cooking'. The action was going on at a past time — when I was in school — so we use the Past Continuous: was + cooking.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'I ______ lunch at 1 o'clock in the afternoon.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'was having'. The book's model answer is: 'I was having lunch at 1 o'clock in the afternoon.' A clock time in the past takes the Past Continuous.

mcqs.q: In the story, the bird was sitting on a tree near a ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a stream. The story begins: 'One day a bird was sitting on a tree near a stream. It was looking down at the water below.' There it saw the ant sinking in the water.

mcqs.q: Complete from the story: 'It saw that an ant ______ in the water.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'was sinking'. All the story verbs are in the Past Continuous because the actions were going on in the past: was sitting, was looking, was sinking, was trying, was flowing.

mcqs.q: Complete from the story: 'The water ______ very fast.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'was flowing'. The ant was trying to get out, 'but the water was flowing very fast.' The bird then dropped a leaf in the water to save the ant.

mcqs.q: How did the bird save the ant?
options: By dropping a leaf in the water near the ant
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: by dropping a leaf in the water near the ant. The ant climbed on the leaf, and later the ant repaid the kindness by biting the hunter who was going to shoot the bird.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentences.
options: They have a dog, a cat, and two hens next year they will buy a goat and a cow
They have a dog, a cat, and two hens. Next year they will buy a goat and a cow.
they have a dog, a cat, and two hens. next year they will buy a goat and a cow.
They have a dog a cat and two hens. Next year, they will buy a goat and a cow
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the second one. It has two proper sentences: the first ends with a full stop, and 'Next year' begins with a capital letter. This is the book's own punctuation exercise.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct pair of sentences.
options: My sister's parrot can say a few words i like the way it talks
My sister's parrot can say a few words. I like the way it talks.
my sister's parrot can say a few words. i like the way it talks.
My sister's parrot can say a few words I like the way it talks.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'My sister's parrot can say a few words. I like the way it talks.' Each sentence starts with a capital letter — note that the pronoun 'I' is always written with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: In the Imdad and Salim passage, why did Salim start crying?
options: His name was very long — Salimuddin Kochriwala — so writing it one thousand times would take him much longer than Imdad Khan
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: his name was very long. Salim said, 'My name is Salimuddin Kochriwala and his name is Imdad Khan. He will finish very quickly.' The teacher had told both boys to write their full names one thousand times.

lessons.title: Writing: Describing an Object
lessons.notes_html:
Describing an Object

We guess and describe objects by their clues: size, shape, colour, use, and what they are made of. First read the book's examples:

  • All students have it. It is made of paper. People read it. — It's a book.
  • It takes people from place to place. It has wheels and it plies on roads. It makes a lot of noise. — It's a rickshaw.
  • It is sharp and has a handle. People use it to cut things in the kitchen. — It's a knife.
  • It is sweet and soft. It comes in summer. It grows on trees. — It's a mango.
  • It is easy to carry. People use it to make calls. — It's a mobile phone.
  • They have sharp and pointed ends. They are used to cut wires, paper or cloth. — They're a pair of scissors.
  • Sometimes it is put on a wall. We can tell the time by looking at it. — It's a clock.
  • People travel on it. It runs on rails. It takes people from one city to another. — It's a train.

Headings for Describing an Object

  • Name of object — e.g. table
  • Size — small / medium / large
  • Shape — square / rectangle / round
  • Colour — e.g. brown
  • Smell / Taste — if it has any
  • Texture (feel) — hard / smooth / soft / rough
  • Use — what we do with it

Example — chair: Size: medium. Shape: square. Colour: brown. Smell: wood. Texture: hard/smooth. Use: sitting.

Describing Our Classroom (Model)

'My classroom is big and clean. There are twenty desks and twenty chairs in it. There is a table and a chair for the teacher. There is a blackboard and a cupboard. The windows are big and fresh air comes through them. We clean our classroom daily and throw rubbish in the dustbin.'

mcqs.q: 'It is made of paper. All students have it. People read it.' What is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a book. This is the book's own worked example in 'Describing an Object'. The clues — made of paper, all students have it, people read it — all point to a book.

mcqs.q: 'It has wheels, plies on roads and makes a lot of noise. It takes people from place to place.' What is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a rickshaw. A train also takes people from place to place, but it runs on rails, not on roads. The rickshaw plies on roads and makes a lot of noise.

mcqs.q: 'It is sharp and has a handle. People use it to cut things in the kitchen. Children are not allowed to use it.' What is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a knife. The clues are: sharp, has a handle, used to cut things in the kitchen. Scissors are used to cut wires, paper or cloth, not kitchen things.

mcqs.q: 'It is sweet and soft. It comes in summer. Sometimes it is orange and sometimes yellow. It grows on trees.' What is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a mango. The description matches the mango exactly — sweet and soft, a summer fruit, orange or yellow in colour, and it grows on trees.

mcqs.q: 'It is easy to carry. Many people have it these days. People use it to make calls.' What is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a mobile phone. It is small and easy to carry, and its use — making calls — gives the answer. Description clues always include the use of the object.

mcqs.q: 'They have sharp and pointed ends. They are used to cut wires, paper or cloth.' What are they?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a pair of scissors. Note the plural clues — 'They have', 'They are used' — because scissors are spoken of as a pair. They cut wires, paper or cloth.

mcqs.q: 'People travel on it. It runs on rails. It takes people from one city to another.' What is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a train. The special clue is 'It runs on rails.' A rickshaw runs on roads, and a bus also runs on roads, but only a train runs on rails.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT one of the headings used to describe an object?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: price of the object. The book's headings are: name, size, shape, colour, smell, taste, texture (feel) and use. We do not need to fill all the headings, and price is not one of them.

mcqs.q: In the model description of a chair, its texture (feel) is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: hard/smooth. The model says: Chair — Size: medium, Shape: square, Colour: brown, Smell: wood, Texture (feel): hard/smooth, Use: sitting. Texture tells us how a thing feels when we touch it.

mcqs.q: According to the model paragraph, how many desks and chairs are there in the classroom?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: twenty desks and twenty chairs. The model paragraph says, 'There are twenty desks and twenty chairs in it. There is a table and a chair for the teacher.' When we describe our own classroom, we write the real numbers of our room.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Self-Created Cloze and Book Covers
lessons.notes_html:
Self-Created Cloze — Keep Practising

Remember to do the Self-Created Cloze every day, as explained in Unit 1, section 1.5:

  • Choose a paragraph and mark every 8th word.
  • Copy the paragraph in a separate notebook with blanks in place of the marked words.
  • Take a break of half an hour, then fill in the blanks without looking.
  • Check with the book and give yourself one mark for each correct answer.

Reading a Book Cover

The cover of a book tells us three important things:

  • The title — the name of the book.
  • The author — the writer of the book.
  • The illustrator — the person who made the design and pictures of the cover.

Example from the Book

  • Title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
  • Author: L. Frank Baum
  • Illustrator: W.W. Denslow

When we look at any book cover, we should be able to find and write its title, its author's name and its illustrator's name.

mcqs.q: The Self-Created Cloze activity in this unit reminds us to do it ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: every day. Section 2.5 says, 'Do you want to speak and write good English? Remember to do the Self-Created Cloze every day.' The steps are the same as in Unit 1, section 1.5.

mcqs.q: In Self-Created Cloze we mark every ______ word of the paragraph.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 8th. We mark every 8th word, copy the paragraph with a blank line in its place, take a break of half an hour, and then fill the blanks without looking at the original paragraph.

mcqs.q: The name of a book, written on its cover, is called its ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: title. The book explains that a cover has the name (title) of the book, the name of the writer (author) and the name of the person who made the design of the cover (illustrator).

mcqs.q: The writer of a book is called the ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: author. For 'The Wonderful Wizard of Oz', the author is L. Frank Baum — he wrote the book. The illustrator only makes the cover design and pictures.

mcqs.q: The person who makes the design of the cover is called the ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: illustrator. For 'The Wonderful Wizard of Oz', the illustrator is W.W. Denslow. He made the design of the cover, while L. Frank Baum wrote the book.

mcqs.q: Who is the author of 'The Wonderful Wizard of Oz'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: L. Frank Baum. This is the book's own example of reading a book cover: Title — The Wonderful Wizard of Oz; Author — L. Frank Baum; Illustrator — W.W. Denslow.

mcqs.q: Who is the illustrator of 'The Wonderful Wizard of Oz'?
options: L. Frank Baum and W.W. Denslow
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: W.W. Denslow. The cover example clearly separates the two jobs: Baum is the author (writer) and Denslow is the illustrator (cover designer).

mcqs.q: Which three things do we write from a book cover in this exercise?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: title, author and illustrator. The exercise says: 'Now look at the books given below and write their titles, author's name and the name of the illustrator below each book.'

mcqs.q: After filling the cloze blanks, we check our work by ______.
options: opening the textbook and comparing answers, giving one mark for each correct answer
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: opening the textbook and comparing, with one mark for each correct answer. This self-checking is part of the Self-Created Cloze steps from Unit 1.5, repeated in every unit.

mcqs.q: Why do we take a break of half an hour in the cloze activity?
options: So that we fill the blanks from our own memory, without looking at the paragraph
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: so that we fill the blanks from our own memory. Step 6 says, 'Close the books. Take a break of half an hour.' After the break we cannot copy — we have to remember and think, which makes our English strong.

lessons.title: Fun: Making a Card
lessons.notes_html:
Making a Get Well Soon Card

Your friend is sick. Make a card that says 'Get well soon'. Draw or paste colourful pictures on it and write a message for your friend.

Wishes We Can Choose From

  • Get well soon. We all miss you.
  • Come on. Get out of bed, come and play with us.
  • Wish you good health.
  • I miss you, my friend. Get well soon.
  • This is to wish you a healthy life.
  • Health is wealth. Take good care of it.

Model Message

'Dear friend, I was sad to hear that you are sick. Get well soon. We all miss you. Health is wealth. Take good care of it. Your friend.'

A good card has colourful pictures, a kind message, and the name of the sender at the end. This activity fits the unit's theme — understanding physical well being and taking care of our health.

mcqs.q: In this Fun activity, we make a card for ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a sick friend. The book says, 'Your friend is sick. Make a card that says get well soon.' We draw or paste colourful pictures and write a kind message on it.

mcqs.q: What is written in big words on the card?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Get Well Soon. The card is made to make a sick friend happy and to wish him good health so that he can come back and play with us.

mcqs.q: Which of these wishes is in the book's list?
options: Health is wealth. Take good care of it
Best of luck for the exam
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Health is wealth. Take good care of it.' It is one of the six wishes given in the book. The others, like 'Get well soon. We all miss you', are also in the list.

mcqs.q: What do we put on the card to make it beautiful?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: colourful pictures, drawn or pasted. The book says, 'Draw or paste colourful pictures. Write a message for your friend.' Pictures make the card cheerful for a sick friend.

mcqs.q: Which wish tells the friend that everyone is waiting for him?
options: Come on. Get out of bed
This is to wish you a healthy life
Get well soon. We all miss you
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Get well soon. We all miss you.' This wish tells the sick friend that his friends miss him. Such kind words make a sick person feel happy and loved.

mcqs.q: 'Health is wealth' means ______.
options: good health is more valuable than money
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: good health is more valuable than money. This famous saying is in the book's wish list. It matches the whole unit, which teaches us how to stay well and healthy like Kamal decided to do.

mcqs.q: A model message begins with the words ______.
options: Dear friend, I was sad to hear that you are sick
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Dear friend, I was sad to hear that you are sick.' The model message then says, 'Get well soon. We all miss you. Health is wealth. Take good care of it. Your friend.'

mcqs.q: Who signs the card at the end in the model message?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the sender, who signs as 'Your friend.' A card message always ends with the name or sign of the person who is sending the card.

mcqs.q: Which wish invites the friend to come and play?
options: Come on. Get out of bed, come and play with us
This is to wish you a healthy life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Come on. Get out of bed, come and play with us.' It is one of the wishes in the book's list. It cheerfully invites the sick friend to get better and join his friends again.

mcqs.q: Making a card for a sick friend teaches us ______.
options: to care for others and wish them good health
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to care for others and wish them good health. This Fun activity is part of the unit 'Understanding Physical Well Being', so it joins the lesson of health with kindness for a sick friend.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Try Again — A Poem
lessons.notes_html:
The Poem — Try Again (by W.E. Hickson)

'Tis a lesson you should heed, Try again;
If at first you don't succeed, Try again.
Then your courage should appear, For if you will persevere,
You will conquer, never fear, Try again.

Once or twice, though you should fail, Try again;
If you would at last prevail, Try again;
If we strive, 'tis no disgrace, Though we do not win the race;
What should we do in that case? Try again.

If you find your task is hard, Try again;
Time will bring you your reward, Try again;
All that other folks can do, Why, with patience, may not you?
Only keep this rule in view, Try again.

Word Meanings

  • heed — pay attention to
  • persevere — keep on trying
  • conquer — fight and win
  • prevail — win
  • strive — try hard
  • disgrace — something to be ashamed of
  • task — work
  • reward — gift for doing something good
  • keep in view — remember

Key Points

  • The poem has three verses. The words 'Try again' are repeated 9 times.
  • Rhyming words: heed–succeed–feed; fail–prevail–sail; hard–reward–card; appear–persevere–fear–near; disgrace–race–case–face; do–you–view–too.
  • The message: if we do not succeed at first, we should not give up. With patience, we can do all that other folks can do.

mcqs.q: How many verses are there in the poem 'Try Again'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The poem has three verses, and each verse teaches the same lesson in a new way: try again if you fail, try again if the task is hard, and time will bring your reward.

mcqs.q: How many times are the words 'Try again' repeated in the poem?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is nine times. Every verse ends its lines with 'Try again', and across the three verses the phrase comes nine times in total. It is the heart of the poem.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the poem 'Try Again'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is W.E. Hickson. The poet's name is given at the end of the poem in the textbook: '(W.E. Hickson)'.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'heed' mean in the poem?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: pay attention to. The first line, ''Tis a lesson you should heed', means: this is a lesson you should pay attention to. The vocabulary exercise matches 'heed' with 'pay attention to'.

mcqs.q: What does 'persevere' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: keep on trying. The line 'For if you will persevere, you will conquer, never fear' means that if we keep on trying, we will surely win in the end.

mcqs.q: What does 'conquer' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: fight and win. In the vocabulary table, 'conquer' is matched with 'fight and win', and 'prevail' is matched with 'win'. Both words promise success to the person who tries again.

mcqs.q: What does 'disgrace' mean?
options: A gift for doing something good
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: something to be ashamed of. The poem says, 'If we strive, 'tis no disgrace' — trying hard is never something to be ashamed of, even if we do not win the race.

mcqs.q: Which line is from Verse 1 of the poem?
options: If you find your task is hard
Time will bring you your reward
Once or twice, though you should fail
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: ''Tis a lesson you should heed'. It is the very first line of Verse 1. 'Once or twice, though you should fail' opens Verse 2, and 'Time will bring you your reward' is in Verse 3.

mcqs.q: 'Time will bring you your reward' is a line of which verse?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Verse 3. In the book's exercise, this line's verse number is 3. Verse 3 also says: 'If you find your task is hard, Try again' and 'Only keep this rule in view, Try again.'

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with 'heed' in the poem?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'succeed'. The rhyming-words table gives: heed — succeed — feed. All three words end with the same sound, which makes the poem musical.

mcqs.q: Which set of words rhyme together in the poem?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: fail — prevail — sail. This is Table 1 of the rhyming exercise. The other sets mix words from different rhyming groups.

mcqs.q: What is the main message of the poem?
options: We should never try difficult work
If we do not succeed at first, we should try again and not give up
We should always win the race
We should wait for others to help us
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: if we do not succeed at first, we should try again and not give up. The summary of the poem says: 'If we fail once or twice, we should try again... Time will bring us our reward.'

mcqs.q: According to the poem, what can we do with patience?
options: All that other folks can do
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: all that other folks can do. The last verse asks: 'All that other folks can do, Why, with patience, may not you?' This is why the unit is named 'Patience'.

mcqs.q: 'If we strive, 'tis no disgrace, Though we do not win the race.' This line is in ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Verse 2. In the matching exercise, the explanation 'If we try hard it is nothing to be ashamed of' is matched with this line of Verse 2.

mcqs.q: The word 'reward' in the poem means ______.
options: a gift for doing something good
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a gift for doing something good. The vocabulary table matches 'reward' with 'gift for doing something good'. The poem promises: 'Time will bring you your reward.'

lessons.title: Speaking: Agree or Disagree Politely
lessons.notes_html:
Agree or Disagree Politely

In this section, three students roleplay a dialogue about going to Murree. They agree and disagree with each other politely.

Useful Phrases

  • I think... — to give our own idea: 'I think it's a great idea.'
  • I don't agree with you — to disagree politely: 'I don't agree with you, Nadeem.'
  • You have a point — to accept part of another's idea: 'You have a point. If you don't like the cold weather you will not be able to enjoy yourself.'
  • Yes, but... — to add another side: 'Yes, but many of us want to see the snow.'

The Dialogue — Key Points

  • Nadeem: Going to Murree in January is a stupid idea. He hates the cold weather.
  • Sameer: He does not agree; he thinks it is a great idea, but he also accepts Nadeem's point.
  • Saleh: Many of us want to see the snow. That is why we want to go in January.
  • Saleh's solution: This year we can go in January and next year we can go in June.

After the roleplay, we discuss our own village/town/city — what is good or bad in it — using the same phrases.

mcqs.q: What is the dialogue in this section about?
options: Going to Murree — in January or in summer
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: going to Murree — in January or in summer. Nadeem, Sameer and Saleh discuss the trip and agree and disagree politely with one another.

mcqs.q: Who says, 'Going to Murree in January is a stupid idea'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Nadeem. He speaks the first line of the dialogue. Sameer then disagrees politely: 'I don't agree with you, Nadeem. I think it's a great idea.'

mcqs.q: Why does Nadeem not want to go to Murree in January?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: he hates the cold weather. Nadeem says, 'I hate the cold weather. If we go there in the summer we can really enjoy ourselves.' January in Murree is very cold and snowy.

mcqs.q: Who wants to go in January to see the snow?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Saleh and many others. Saleh says, 'Yes, but many of us want to see the snow. That's why we want to go in January.' He uses 'Yes, but' to add his side politely.

mcqs.q: Which phrase shows polite disagreement?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'I don't agree with you.' Sameer uses it with Nadeem's name: 'I don't agree with you, Nadeem. I think it's a great idea.' This is the polite way taught in this section — the name of the section itself is 'Agree or Disagree Politely'.

mcqs.q: What does 'You have a point' mean?
options: You are standing at a point
Your idea has some truth in it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: your idea has some truth in it. Sameer says, 'You have a point. If you don't like the cold weather you will not be able to enjoy yourself.' He accepts part of Nadeem's view before giving his own.

mcqs.q: What solution does Saleh give at the end?
options: Go in January this year and in June next year
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: go in January this year and in June next year. Saleh says, 'Tell you what, this year we can go in January and next year we can go in June.' A good solution makes both sides happy.

mcqs.q: How many students roleplay this dialogue together?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The book says, 'In groups of three, roleplay the following dialogue,' and each student plays all three roles — Nadeem, Sameer and Saleh — by changing roles.

mcqs.q: What does Nadeem think is more fun than playing with snowballs?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: playing with a cricket ball. Nadeem says, 'I think, playing with a cricket ball is much more fun than playing with snowballs.' Sameer replies that different people like different things.

mcqs.q: After the roleplay, students discuss their own village/town/city. They talk about ______.
options: what is good or bad in their own place
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: what is good or bad in their own place. The solved answer says: 'Then discuss your village/town/city: what is good or bad in it. Use phrases like I think, I agree/don't agree, You have a point, Yes, but, etc.'

lessons.title: Language Practice: Nouns — Singular and Plural
lessons.notes_html:
Nouns — Singular and Plural

A noun names a person, place, animal or thing. Most nouns make their plural by adding -s or -es. Some plurals are different.

  • sister — sisters; cage — cages; holiday — holidays
  • watch — watches; fox — foxes; dash — dashes; match — matches
  • shelf — shelves; wife — wives
  • tomato — tomatoes; buffalo — buffaloes; mosquito — mosquitoes
  • fairy — fairies; berry — berries
  • person — people; tooth — teeth; child — children; man — men; woman — women; foot — feet
  • hair — hair; sheep — sheep; fish — fish (these do not change)

Choosing the Correct Number

  • How many people are there in the bus?
  • Five women opened a school.
  • Every child enjoys learning through pictures.
  • Most cricket players are more than five feet tall.
  • The boys caught ten fish and five crabs.

Changing Sentences to Plural

When we change a sentence to plural, we change the noun, the verb and the pronouns as needed.

  • A baby cow is called a calf. → Baby cows are called calves.
  • I saw an ox in the field. → We saw oxen in the fields.
  • There is a sheep in the barn. → There are sheep in the barns.
  • My knife is on the table. → My knives are on the tables.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'watch'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'watches'. Nouns ending in -ch take -es in the plural: watch–watches, match–matches. In the same way fox–foxes and dash–dashes take -es.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'shelf'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'shelves'. Some nouns ending in -f change the f to v and add -es: shelf–shelves, wife–wives. The book's example says: 'The young women put the things on the shelves.'

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'person'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'people'. 'Person' has a special plural: person–people. The book's sentence is: 'How many people are there in the bus?'

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'tooth'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'teeth'. Tooth is an irregular noun: tooth–teeth, like foot–feet and man–men. These plurals must be remembered.

mcqs.q: Which noun does NOT change in the plural?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'sheep'. Sheep stays 'sheep' in both singular and plural: 'There is a sheep in the barn' → 'There are sheep in the barns.' Hair and fish also do not change.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'fairy'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'fairies'. When a noun ends in a consonant + y, we change y to i and add -es: fairy–fairies, berry–berries. But 'holiday' becomes 'holidays' because a vowel (a) comes before the y.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Five women opened a school.' 'Woman' has the special plural 'women', and after 'five' we need the plural. 'A school' stays singular because only one school was opened.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Most cricket player are more than five foot tall.
Most cricket players are more than five feet tall.
Most cricket players is more than five foots tall.
Most cricket player is more than five feet tall.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Most cricket players are more than five feet tall.' We need plurals 'players' and 'feet' (plural of foot), and the plural verb 'are'.

mcqs.q: Change to plural: 'I saw an ox in the field.'
options: I saw oxes in the field.
We saw oxen in the fields.
I saw an oxen in the field.
We saw oxes in the fields.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'We saw oxen in the fields.' The book's solved answer changes I→We, ox→oxen and field→fields. When we change the number, we change nouns, verbs and pronouns as needed.

mcqs.q: Change to plural: 'My knife is on the table.'
options: My knives is on the tables.
My knives are on the tables.
My knifes are on the table.
My knife are on the tables.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'My knives are on the tables.' Knife becomes knives (f changes to v), 'is' becomes 'are', and 'the table' becomes 'the tables'. All parts of the sentence must agree.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Cohesive Devices and Punctuation
lessons.notes_html:
Cohesive Devices — But and Unlike

But joins two parts of a sentence that have opposite or different ideas.

  • We are late but we will catch the train.
  • We are having a good time but we miss some of our friends.
  • I worked hard for the test but I didn't pass.
  • Qurban has three goats but he wants a cow.

Unlike shows that two people or things are different from each other. It usually comes at the start of the sentence.

  • Unlike Samina, Najma loves driving.
  • Unlike Badin, the weather in Murree is quite cold.
  • Unlike coins, we can fold the paper money.
  • Unlike Hyderabad, Bhambhore has no shopping plazas.

Punctuation — Capital Letters and Question Marks

Questions begin with a capital letter, end with a question mark (?), and names of people, places, months and days take capital letters.

  • Are you ill?
  • Why are you wearing a sweater in July?
  • May I come in, please?
  • Do you know Arif's address in Quetta?
  • What did you say to Mrs. Chandio on Friday?
  • Is this the book that you bought from Mr. Shah?

mcqs.q: Complete: 'We are late ______ we will catch the train.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'but'. The two ideas are opposite — we are late, yet we will catch the train — so we join them with 'but'. 'Unlike' compares two people or things, it does not join clauses like this.

mcqs.q: Complete: '______ Badin, the weather in Murree is quite cold.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Unlike'. The sentence compares two places, Badin and Murree: 'Unlike Badin, the weather in Murree is quite cold.' Unlike shows difference between two things.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'I worked hard for the test ______ I didn't pass.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'but'. Working hard and not passing are opposite results, so they are joined with 'but'. This is from the book's matching exercise.

mcqs.q: Complete: '______ coins, we can fold the paper money.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Unlike'. Coins cannot be folded, but paper money can. 'Unlike coins' compares paper money with coins at the start of the sentence.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct question.
