mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Are you ill?' A question begins with a capital letter (A) and ends with a question mark. This is the first sentence of the book's punctuation exercise.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct question.
options: Why are you wearing a sweater in july
Why are you wearing a sweater in July.
why are you wearing a sweater in July?
Why are you wearing a sweater in July?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Why are you wearing a sweater in July?' The month 'July' takes a capital letter, the sentence starts with a capital W, and a question ends with a question mark.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct question.
options: Do you know arif's address in quetta?
Do you know Arif's address in quetta.
do you know Arif's address in Quetta.
Do you know Arif's address in Quetta?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Do you know Arif's address in Quetta?' Names of people (Arif) and places (Quetta) begin with capital letters, and the question mark ends the question.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct question.
options: what did you say to Mrs. Chandio on friday?
What did you say to mrs. chandio on Friday
What did you say to Mrs. Chandio on Friday?
What did you said to Mrs. Chandio on Friday?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'What did you say to Mrs. Chandio on Friday?' 'Mrs.' and 'Chandio' are a person's name and title, 'Friday' is a day — all take capitals — and the sentence is a question, so it ends with '?'.

mcqs.q: 'Unlike Hyderabad, Bhambhore has no shopping plazas.' In this sentence, 'Unlike' compares ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: two places — Hyderabad and Bhambhore. This is the book's worked example for the but/unlike matching exercise. Unlike is used to show how one place is different from another.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Lahore has a river ______ Karachi has the sea.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'but'. The complete sentence from the exercise is: 'Lahore has a river but Karachi has the sea.' The two facts are different, so 'but' joins them inside one sentence.

lessons.title: Writing: Describing an Animal
lessons.notes_html:
Describing an Animal

We describe an animal by its body, its home, its food and its habits. First, guess the animal from the clues:

  • It has a hump on its back. It lives in deserts. — camel
  • It swims in the water. It has feathers. — duck
  • It is kept as a pet. It eats grass. — goat
  • It does not sleep at night. It has round eyes. — owl
  • It has wings but cannot fly. It lays eggs. — hen
  • It lives in mountains and on trees. It likes to eat bananas. — monkey
  • It has four legs and lines on its body. It eats meat. — tiger

Table for Writing a Description

  • Fish — Colour: many colours; Body parts: gills to breathe, fins to swim; Skin: scales; Food: plants, small fish, worms; Home: lake, sea, pond; Young: fry.
  • Elephant — Colour: grey, red, brown, black; Body parts: tusks (teeth), trunk (nose), fan-like ears; Skin: thick, rough; Food: grass, leaves, fruit; Home: forests, mountains, deserts; Young: calf.
  • Lizard — Colour: many colours; Body parts: long tail, long tongue, four short legs; Skin: scales, no hair; Food: insects; Home: warm places; Young: hatchling.
  • Squirrel — Colour: brown, grey, red, black, white; Body parts: cheeks to store food, long bushy tail, pads on feet to jump on trees, sharp teeth; Food: nuts, roots, leaves, plants; Home: tree holes, deserts; Young: baby.

Sample Description — Fish

'Fish live in water. Their skin is covered with scales. They swim with the help of fins and breathe through gills. They lay eggs in water and their young are called fry. They eat small plants and worms. Some large fish eat the small fish.'

After writing, we show our description to another group. They check our spellings (Sp), grammar (G) and punctuation (P), and we rewrite if there are errors.

mcqs.q: 'It has a hump on its back. It lives in deserts.' Which animal is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: camel. The hump on the back and life in the desert are the special clues of the camel. This is the book's worked example in 'Describing an Animal'.

mcqs.q: 'It swims in the water. It has feathers.' Which animal is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: duck. A fish swims but has no feathers. The duck swims in water and has feathers, so it is the answer.

mcqs.q: 'It does not sleep at night. It has round eyes.' Which animal is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: owl. The owl stays awake at night and has big round eyes. The hen and the cat sleep at night.

mcqs.q: 'It has wings but cannot fly. It lays eggs.' Which animal is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: hen. A hen has wings but cannot fly, and it lays eggs. A crow can fly well, so it does not match the clues.

mcqs.q: 'It has four legs and lines on its body. It eats meat.' Which animal is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: tiger. The lines (stripes) on its body and eating meat are the tiger's clues. A goat eats grass, not meat.

mcqs.q: The young of a fish is called a ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: fry. The book's table says: Fish — Young: fry. The elephant's young is a calf, and the lizard's young is a hatchling.

mcqs.q: The young of an elephant is called a ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: calf. In the description table, Elephant — Young: calf. The elephant also has tusks, a trunk and fan-like ears, and its skin is thick and rough.

mcqs.q: Fish breathe through their ______ and swim with their ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: gills; fins. The sample description says: 'They swim with the help of fins and breathe through gills.' Their skin is covered with scales.

mcqs.q: A squirrel stores food in its ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: cheeks. The table says the squirrel has 'cheeks to store food', a long bushy tail, pads on feet to jump on trees, and sharp teeth. It eats nuts, roots, leaves and plants.

mcqs.q: When another group checks our description, the marks Sp, G and P stand for ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Spelling, Grammar, Punctuation. The book says: 'Show your description to another group to make corrections on spellings (Sp), grammar (G) and punctuation (P). Rewrite if there are errors.'

lessons.title: Study Skills: Alphabetical Order and Self-Created Cloze
lessons.notes_html:
Alphabetical Order

Book covers — and words in a dictionary — are arranged in alphabetical order: the order of the letters A to Z. We arrange titles by the first letter of their names. Titles beginning with A come first, then B, then C, and so on.

Self-Created Cloze — Daily Practice

Remember to do the Cloze activity explained in Unit 1, section 1.5, daily:

  • Choose a paragraph from your English textbook or any other English book.
  • Mark every 8th word and copy the paragraph with blank lines in a separate notebook.
  • Draw a margin, put the date, and write neatly.
  • Take a break of half an hour.
  • Fill in the blanks without looking at the original paragraph.
  • Open the book, check your answers, and give yourself one mark for each correct answer.

Doing this every day will make your reading, spelling and writing strong.

mcqs.q: In alphabetical order, we arrange names by ______.
options: the first letter of their names
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the first letter of their names. The solved answer for the book-cover exercise says: 'Arrange the book covers in the alphabetical order of the first letter of their titles.'

mcqs.q: Which title comes FIRST in alphabetical order?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Animal Stories'. It begins with A, which comes before M (My School), T (The Park Rules) and Z (Zoo Visit) in the alphabet.

mcqs.q: Which title comes LAST in alphabetical order?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Zoo Visit'. Z is the last letter of the alphabet, so a title beginning with Z comes after A, M and T titles.

mcqs.q: Alphabetical order is also used in ______.
options: a dictionary, to find words quickly
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a dictionary. Dictionaries arrange words from A to Z so we can find any word quickly. The same skill helps us arrange book covers and names.

mcqs.q: The Self-Created Cloze must be done ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: daily. Section 3.5 says, 'Remember to do the Cloze activity explained in Unit 1.5, daily.' Every unit of this book repeats this study skill.

mcqs.q: In the cloze activity, after copying the paragraph we take a break of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: half an hour. Then we fill the blanks without looking at the original paragraph. The break makes the activity a real test of memory and understanding.

mcqs.q: How many marks do we give for each correct blank in the cloze?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: one mark. The steps of Unit 1.5 end with: 'Give yourself one mark for each correct answer.' We check our own work honestly.

mcqs.q: The cloze paragraph is copied in ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a separate notebook. The activity needs an extra notebook, in which we draw a margin, write the date, and copy the paragraph in our best handwriting with blanks for every 8th word.

mcqs.q: Which of these do we check before filling the cloze blanks? 'Have you put in a ______ and the date?'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: margin. The check list of Unit 1.5 asks: 'Have you put in a margin? Have you put in the date? Have you started the paragraph two-finger space away from the margin?'

mcqs.q: Study skills like alphabetical order and cloze help us to ______.
options: learn and find things in an organised way
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: learn and find things in an organised way. Study Skills sections teach us how to learn by ourselves: arranging in alphabetical order helps us find books and words, and daily cloze practice improves our English.

lessons.title: Fun: Our Newspaper
lessons.notes_html:
Our Newspaper

In groups of 3, on a large sheet, make a two-page newspaper.

What Our Newspaper Should Cover

  • Any international news
  • At least one national news
  • A local news
  • Sports news
  • Weather for today in your area
  • Prayer timings for today
  • Any two interesting advertisements

Guidelines

  • Give your newspaper a name.
  • Collect a few newspapers and use them as a guide.
  • Don't forget to write the headlines.
  • Write the day and date.
  • Draw or paste pictures to make the front page colourful.
  • Write each article in a separate box. Don't write more than 100 words.
  • Once you have written your newspaper, put it up in the classroom.

Model

Newspaper name: 'Our School News'. Headline: 'Cleanliness Campaign in Our School'. News: 'A cleanliness campaign was held in our school. All the students took part. Our school is now clean and beautiful.'

mcqs.q: How many pages should 'Our Newspaper' have?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is two pages. The Fun section says: 'In groups of 3, on a large sheet, make a two-page newspaper.' It should look like a real newspaper with headlines and boxes.

mcqs.q: How many students work together on one newspaper?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The activity begins: 'In groups of 3...' The three students collect news, write articles and draw pictures together.

mcqs.q: Which of these must our newspaper include?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: sports news. The newspaper should cover international news, at least one national news, a local news, sports news, weather, prayer timings and two advertisements.

mcqs.q: How many advertisements should the newspaper have?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: two interesting advertisements. The list says 'any two interesting advertisements'. Advertisements are a real part of every newspaper.

mcqs.q: How many words should one article have at most?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 100 words. The guideline says: 'Write each article in a separate box. Don't write more than 100 words.' Short articles are easy to read.

mcqs.q: What must we not forget to write for each news item?
options: The name of the writer's school
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the headline. The guideline says, 'Don't forget to write the headlines.' A headline is the big title that tells readers what the news is about.

mcqs.q: What do we write on the newspaper along with the news?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the day and date. The guidelines say, 'Write the day and date.' Every real newspaper shows its day and date at the top.

mcqs.q: How do we make the front page colourful?
options: By writing in many colours only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: by drawing or pasting pictures. The guideline says, 'Draw or paste pictures to make the front page colourful.' Pictures attract readers to the news.

mcqs.q: When the newspaper is ready, where do we put it up?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in the classroom. The last guideline says, 'Once you have written your newspaper, put it up in the classroom.' Then the whole class can read it.

mcqs.q: In the model, the headline 'Cleanliness Campaign in Our School' is for a ______ news.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: local/school news. The model newspaper 'Our School News' reports: 'A cleanliness campaign was held in our school. All the students took part.' News about our own school and area is local news.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Diary Entry — Shahban's Day
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Shahban is a young boy who lives in Badin, Sindh. His father wants him to become a great man, so he wants Shahban to study well and to work hard. Shahban goes to school daily, always does his homework on time, and writes what he does every day in his diary.

Shahban's Diary — Monday, 02.02.2017

  • He goes to school in the mornings and comes back home at 1 o'clock in the afternoon.
  • He says his prayers, has lunch, helps his elder sister clean the home, and she helps him with his homework.
  • After that, he goes for his Quran classes.
  • In the evening he works at the Allahwala Milk Shop, a shop near his house, for two hours every day. He does not work on Sundays and public holidays.
  • The shop owner is a nice man. He says young people should also have time to play with their friends.
  • Father believes that we should work hard and honestly. Mother says that when we keep ourselves busy, we stay away from bad company and bad habits.
  • His boss says that if he works hard, he can have his own milk-shop when he grows up. Shahban's dream job is to be a computer engineer, and he will save money to buy a computer.
  • His grandmother is upset with his parents for making him work. She says he is only eleven years old and should play more.
  • He is learning how to set yoghurt in a clay pot.
  • Every day, after dinner and Isha prayers, he goes to bed at 9:30.

Word Opposites from the Text

morning–evening, clean–dirty, free–busy, happy–sad, bad–good, honestly–dishonestly, early–late, day–night, able–unable, buy–sell.

Shahban's Daily Routine (in order)

1. He comes back from school at one o'clock. 2. He helps his sister clean the house. 3. He does his homework. 4. He goes to the Quran class. 5. He works at the milk shop for two hours. 6. He sleeps at 9:30.

mcqs.q: What is the name of the diary writer?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Shahban. The diary page begins: 'Name: Shahban, Day: Monday, Date: 02.02.2017.' Shahban writes in his diary what he does every day.

mcqs.q: On which day and date did Shahban write this diary page?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Monday, 02.02.2017. These details are written at the top of the diary entry itself, and they are the book's first reading questions.

mcqs.q: Where is Shahban from?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Badin, Sindh. The introduction says, 'Shahban is a young boy who lives in Badin, Sindh.' At the end of the diary he writes, 'It's 9:30 in Badin now.'

mcqs.q: At what time does Shahban go to bed?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 9:30 at night. He writes: 'Every day, after dinner and Isha prayers, I go to bed early to get up early... It's 9:30 in Badin now. I'm off to bed.'

mcqs.q: Where does Shahban work in the evening?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: at the Allahwala Milk Shop. The book's correction exercise makes this clear: 'He works in a milk shop' (not a medical store), and the shop is near his house.

mcqs.q: For how many hours does Shahban work every day?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is two hours. His father spoke to the owner 'to allow me to work there... for two hours every day', and Shahban does not work on Sundays and public holidays.

mcqs.q: Why did the owner give Shahban a holiday on Sundays and public holidays?
options: Because Shahban asked for more pay
Because young people should also have time to play with their friends
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because young people should also have time to play with their friends. The owner is a nice man; he agreed to the holidays for this kind reason.

mcqs.q: What two things does Shahban's father think people should do?
options: Save money and buy a shop
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: work hard and honestly. The diary says, 'Father believes that we should work hard and honestly.' This is the main lesson of the unit, 'The Value of Labour'.

mcqs.q: Why is Shahban's grandmother upset?
options: Because he goes to bed late
Because he wants to buy a computer
Because his parents made him work at only eleven years old; she thinks he should play more
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because his parents made him work at only eleven years old. The diary says, 'My grandmother is upset with my parents for making me work. She says I am only eleven years old and that I should play more.'

mcqs.q: What is Shahban learning to make at the milk shop?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: yoghurt in a clay pot. He writes, 'I am learning how to set yoghurt in a clay pot. So, I will be able to make yoghurt for my family very soon.'

mcqs.q: What is Shahban's aim in life?
options: To be a milk shop owner only
To be a shopkeeper in Badin
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to be a computer engineer. The correction exercise tells us: 'Shahban's aim in life is to be a computer engineer' — not only a milk shop owner. He hopes to save enough money to buy a computer for himself.

mcqs.q: In which part of the day does Shahban work?
options: In the evening, after his Quran classes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in the evening, after his Quran classes. His day order is: school in the morning, home at 1 o'clock, prayers and lunch, cleaning and homework, Quran classes, then work at the milk shop.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of 'honestly' from the text's word list?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'dishonestly'. The vocabulary exercise matches opposites: honestly–dishonestly, able–unable, buy–sell, morning–evening, free–busy.

mcqs.q: What does Shahban do first after coming back from school at one o'clock, in his routine order?
options: He helps his sister clean the house
He goes to the Quran class
He works at the milk shop
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: he helps his sister clean the house. The book's ordering exercise gives: 1. comes back from school, 2. helps his sister clean the house, 3. does his homework, 4. Quran class, 5. milk shop, 6. sleeps at 9:30.

mcqs.q: Is the writer happy or sad? Why?
options: Sad, because he has to work
Happy, because he can help his parents by earning money, he is learning work, and he will save money to buy a computer
Sad, because his grandmother is upset
Happy, because he does not go to school
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: happy. Shahban writes, 'I am feeling very happy. Now, I too can help my parents in making our lives better by earning some money.' He is also learning work and saving for a computer.

lessons.title: Speaking: Request and Respond to a Request
lessons.notes_html:
Request and Respond to a Request

In this section, one student plays Kumar and the other plays Zaman. Kumar makes requests, and Zaman responds with helpful ideas. Then we change roles and repeat the dialogue.

The Dialogue — Key Lines

  • Kumar: Zaman, please tell me some things that I can do at home which will make my mother happy.
  • Zaman: Sure. There are many things that you can do.
  • Zaman: You can wash up the dishes after lunch or dinner.
  • Zaman: You can help her by hanging out clothes to dry or by feeding the chickens.
  • Zaman: You can also make your mother happy by keeping your books and clothes in their proper place.
  • Kumar: Thank you, Zaman, for giving me such good ideas.

Key Points

We make a polite request with words like 'please tell me' and 'please give me'. We respond to a request with helpful suggestions: 'You can...' At the end, we thank the person: 'Thank you for giving me such good ideas.' More suggestions from the book: 'You can polish your younger brother's shoes' or 'You can read the newspaper for your grandfather.'

mcqs.q: What does Kumar ask Zaman?
options: To tell him some things he can do at home to make his mother happy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to tell him some things he can do at home to make his mother happy. Kumar's request is: 'Zaman, please tell me some things that I can do at home which will make my mother happy.'

mcqs.q: Which of these does Zaman suggest first?
options: Wash up the dishes after lunch or dinner
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: wash up the dishes after lunch or dinner. Zaman says, 'You can wash up the dishes after lunch or dinner.' Then he adds hanging out clothes and feeding the chickens.

mcqs.q: Zaman also suggests hanging out clothes to dry and ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: feeding the chickens. Zaman says, 'You can help her by hanging out clothes to dry or by feeding the chickens.' These are small helpful jobs at home.

mcqs.q: How else can Kumar make his mother happy, according to Zaman?
options: By keeping his books and clothes in their proper place
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: by keeping his books and clothes in their proper place. Zaman says, 'You can also make your mother happy by keeping your books and clothes in their proper place.' Neatness at home makes mothers happy.

mcqs.q: Which words make Kumar's request polite?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Please tell me.' This section is 'Request and Respond to Request'. Adding 'please' makes a request polite, and Zaman responds happily: 'Sure. There are many things that you can do.'

mcqs.q: How does Zaman respond to the request?
options: He responds with helpful suggestions — 'You can...'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: he responds with helpful suggestions. Zaman's answers all begin with 'You can...' — you can wash up the dishes, you can hang out clothes, you can feed the chickens.

mcqs.q: What does Kumar say at the end?
options: Thank you, Zaman, for giving me such good ideas
I will not do these things
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Thank you, Zaman, for giving me such good ideas.' Thanking the person is the polite way to end a request dialogue.

mcqs.q: Which is another suggestion given in the book for more practice?
options: You can polish your younger brother's shoes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'You can polish your younger brother's shoes.' The solved answer says students can give different suggestions, e.g. 'You can polish your younger brother's shoes' or 'You can read the newspaper for your grandfather'.

mcqs.q: After practising the dialogue once, the partners ______.
options: change roles and repeat the dialogue
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: change roles and repeat the dialogue. The book says: first one student plays Kumar and the other Zaman, then change roles and repeat, so both practise making and responding to requests.

mcqs.q: This speaking lesson connects with the unit because ______.
options: it is about a milk shop
helping our parents at home is also valuable work
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: helping our parents at home is also valuable work. The unit is 'The Value of Labour'. Shahban helps his family by working, and Kumar learns to help his mother at home.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Noun Gender
lessons.notes_html:
Noun Gender

Nouns are of four genders:

  • Masculine Gender — for males: uncle, king, husband, son, prince.
  • Feminine Gender — for females: aunt, queen, wife, daughter, princess.
  • Common Gender — for both males and females: baby, child, doctor, friend, neighbour, principal, police officer, parent, singer, teacher, student, cousin.
  • Neuter Gender — for things: apple, book, cup, drum, egg, fan, grass, hammer, pot, train, pen, chair.

Masculine — Feminine (People)

uncle–aunt, king–queen, host–hostess, landlord–landlady, sir–madam, husband–wife, nephew–niece, prince–princess, widower–widow, son–daughter, father–mother, brother–sister.

Masculine — Feminine (Animals)

billy goat–nanny goat, stag (deer)–doe, bull–cow, drake–duck, peacock–peahen, fox–vixen, tiger–tigress, jack (donkey)–jenny, ram (sheep)–ewe, stallion (horse)–mare, lion–lioness, cock–hen.

Changing Gender in Sentences

  • The landlord had eight sons. → The landlady had eight daughters.
  • The wild mare broke the ropes. → The wild stallion broke the ropes.
  • The vixen killed a cock. → The fox killed a hen.
  • Our landlady sold two ewes and one billy goat. → Our landlord sold two rams and one nanny goat.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'king'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'queen'. The book's noun gender table gives: king–queen, prince–princess, uncle–aunt, husband–wife. Each masculine noun has its own feminine word.

mcqs.q: What is the masculine of 'niece'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'nephew'. The pair is nephew–niece. Uncle pairs with aunt, and son pairs with daughter.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'bull'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'cow'. For animals: bull–cow, ram–ewe, stallion–mare, stag–doe. These pairs are given in the book's gender table.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'drake'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'duck'. The pair is drake–duck. A hen pairs with a cock, a peahen with a peacock, and a jenny with a jack (donkey).

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'fox'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'vixen'. Fox–vixen is one of the animal pairs in the table. Tiger–tigress and lion–lioness are different pairs.

mcqs.q: Which of these nouns is of Common Gender?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'teacher'. Common gender nouns can be used for both males and females: baby, child, doctor, friend, neighbour, principal, parent, singer, teacher. A teacher can be a man or a woman.

mcqs.q: Which of these nouns is of Neuter Gender?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'train'. Neuter gender is for things that are neither male nor female: apple, book, cup, drum, egg, fan, grass, hammer, pot, train.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'widower'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'widow'. The pair is widower–widow. In the changing-gender exercise: 'The widower had a mare' becomes 'The widow had a stallion.'

mcqs.q: Change the gender: 'The landlord had eight sons.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'The landlady had eight daughters.' This is the book's own example. Both nouns change: landlord→landlady and sons→daughters.

mcqs.q: Change the gender: 'The vixen killed a cock.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'The fox killed a hen.' Vixen (female) becomes fox (male), and cock (male) becomes hen (female). Every gender noun in the sentence must change.

mcqs.q: What is the masculine of 'mare'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'stallion'. The pair for horses is stallion–mare. In the exercise, 'The wild mare broke the ropes' becomes 'The wild stallion broke the ropes.'

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'peacock'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'peahen'. The pair is peacock–peahen. In the book's sentence: 'The rich prince sent a peacock as a gift to the king' becomes 'The rich princess sent a peahen as a gift to the queen.'

mcqs.q: 'Principal', 'neighbour', 'baby' and 'doctor' are nouns of ______ gender.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: common gender. The book's common gender list is: baby, child, doctor, friend, neighbour, principal, police officer, parent, singer, teacher. They stand for both males and females.

mcqs.q: Change the gender: 'Sir, I cannot come to school tomorrow.'
options: Madam, I cannot come to school tomorrow.
Aunt, I cannot come to school tomorrow.
Queen, I cannot come to school tomorrow.
Landlady, I cannot come to school tomorrow.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Madam, I cannot come to school tomorrow.' The pair is sir–madam. Only the gender word changes; the rest of the sentence stays the same.

mcqs.q: What is the feminine of 'ram'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'ewe'. For sheep: ram–ewe. For goats: billy goat–nanny goat. The book's table keeps animal pairs separate, so we must learn each pair correctly.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Simple Future with Going To and Commas
lessons.notes_html:
Simple Future with 'Going To'

We use am / is / are + going to + verb to talk about future plans.

  • He is going to leave for Lahore at 5 o'clock.
  • She is going to drink tea after this.
  • I am going to visit the flood victims.
  • They are going to have dinner after the game.
  • It is going to rain heavily.

For the negative, we use not going to:

  • He is not going to read the novel after you finish it.
  • We are not going to sleep late.
  • We are not going to watch the TV.

Aftab's Friend — Model Paragraph

'My friend is going to come by bus. I am going to pick my friend from the bus station. He is going to stay with me. We are going to swim in the lake. I am going to take him to the fields. We are going to play many games. He is going to teach me English. We are going to enjoy ourselves.'

Punctuation — Commas in a List

We use commas to separate items in a list, and 'and' comes before the last item.

  • I like to eat eggs, chapati and tomato chutney for breakfast.
  • My favourite colours are blue, red, pink and purple.
  • Amna, Bashir, Sultan and I are playing football.
  • Karamdad wants to visit France, Italy, Germany and China.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'He ______ going to leave for Lahore at 5 o'clock.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'is'. With he/she/it we use 'is going to': 'He is going to leave for Lahore at 5 o'clock.' With 'I' we use 'am going to', and with we/they/you we use 'are going to'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'They ______ going to have dinner after the game.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'are'. 'They' takes 'are going to': 'They are going to have dinner after the game.' This is Simple Future with going to, from the book's table.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'It ______ going to rain heavily.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'is'. For weather we use 'It is going to...': 'It is going to rain heavily.' The table in the book gives this exact sentence.

mcqs.q: Choose the negative sentence.
options: We are going to sleep late.
We not are going to sleep late.
We going to sleep late not.
We are not going to sleep late.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'We are not going to sleep late.' To make 'going to' negative, we put 'not' after am/is/are: are + not + going to. This sentence is from Aftab's paragraph.

mcqs.q: Complete Aftab's paragraph: 'My friend is going to ______ by bus.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'come'. After 'going to' we use the first form of the verb: going to come, going to pick, going to stay. The book's paragraph begins: 'My friend is going to come (come) by bus.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'I am going to ______ my friend from the bus station.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'pick'. The pattern is always: am/is/are + going to + first form of the verb. Aftab says, 'I am going to pick my friend from the bus station.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'We ______ going to swim in the lake.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'are'. 'We' takes 'are going to': 'We are going to swim in the lake.' Aftab plans many activities with his friend from Quetta.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: I like to eat eggs chapati and tomato chutney for breakfast.
I like to eat eggs, chapati and tomato chutney for breakfast.
I like to eat, eggs, chapati, and, tomato chutney for breakfast.
I like to eat eggs chapati, and tomato chutney for breakfast.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the second one. In a list we put commas between the items and 'and' before the last item: eggs, chapati and tomato chutney. No comma is needed before 'and' in these book sentences.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: My favourite colours are blue red pink and purple.
My favourite colours are blue, red pink, and purple.
My favourite colours are blue, red, pink and purple.
My favourite colours are, blue, red, pink and purple.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'My favourite colours are blue, red, pink and purple.' Four colours are listed with commas, and 'and' joins the last colour, purple.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Amna Bashir Sultan and I are playing football.
Amna, Bashir, Sultan and I are playing football.
Amna, Bashir Sultan, and I, are playing football.
Amna Bashir, Sultan and I are playing, football.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Amna, Bashir, Sultan and I are playing football.' The names in the list are separated by commas: Amna, Bashir, Sultan — and then 'and I'.

lessons.title: Writing: Diary Entry
lessons.notes_html:
Writing a Diary Entry

A diary entry tells what happened in one day of our life. It begins like this:

  • Day: ______ Date: ______
  • Name of Person: ______
  • Dear Diary, ...

How to Write It

  • Use the reading text (Shahban's diary) as your guide.
  • Write 3 paragraphs. Start a new paragraph a little away from the margin.
  • First make a mind map about what you want to write in each paragraph.
  • Start with what happened early in the day and finish with what happened last in the evening.
  • Use pronouns such as I, we, us, me.
  • Use interesting adjectives.
  • Write about things that include your family or close friends.
  • Write about your feelings. Explain what made you sad or happy.

Checking Each Other's Work

Exchange your diary page with your partner. Your partner points out mistakes by writing (Sp) for spelling mistakes, (G) for grammar and (P) for punctuation. Correct the mistakes together, rewrite your diary page and submit your work to your teacher.

Model Diary Entry

'Day: Friday. Date: 10.10.2025. Name: Ahmed. Dear Diary, Today was a happy day. I woke up early in the morning, offered Fajr prayer and went to school. In school I learnt all my lessons and played with my friends. In the afternoon I came home, had lunch and did my homework. In the evening I went to the market with my father and helped him. At night I offered Isha prayer and went to bed early. I am very happy today because I did all my work on time.'

mcqs.q: A diary entry begins by writing the ______.
options: day, date and name of the person
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: day, date and name of the person. The book's format is: 'Day: ___, Date: ___, Name of Person: ___, Dear Diary,...' Shahban's page begins the same way.

mcqs.q: How many paragraphs should the diary entry have?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. The guidelines say: 'Write 3 paragraphs. Start a new paragraph a little away from the margin.' Each paragraph covers a part of the day.

mcqs.q: Before writing, we develop a ______ about what to write in each paragraph.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a mind map. The guideline says, 'Develop a mind map about what you want to write in each paragraph.' Planning first makes the diary clear and complete.

mcqs.q: In a diary entry, we start with ______.
options: what happened last in the evening
what happened early in the day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: what happened early in the day. The guideline says, 'Start with what happened early in the day and finish with what happened last in the evening.' A diary follows the order of the day.

mcqs.q: Which pronouns are used in a diary entry?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: I, we, us, me. A diary is written by a person about himself, so the guideline says, 'Use Pronouns such as I, we, us, me.' Shahban also writes his diary in the same way.

mcqs.q: The marks (Sp), (G) and (P) on a partner's diary page mean ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Spelling, Grammar and Punctuation mistakes. The book says partners point out mistakes 'by writing (Sp) for spelling mistakes, (G) for grammar and (P) for punctuation.'

mcqs.q: After correcting the mistakes with our partner, we ______.
options: rewrite the diary page and submit it to the teacher
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: rewrite the diary page and submit it to the teacher. The last guideline step is: 'Correct the mistakes with the help of your partners. Rewrite your diary page and submit your work to your teacher.'

mcqs.q: A diary entry should also tell ______.
options: our feelings — what made us sad or happy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: our feelings. The guideline says, 'Write about your feelings. Explain what made you sad or happy.' Shahban also writes his feelings: 'I am feeling very happy.'

mcqs.q: Which book text is our guide for writing a diary entry?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Shahban's diary entry in section 4.1. The first guideline says, 'Use the reading text as your guide.' We copy its style: day, date, 'Dear Diary', and the day's events in order.

mcqs.q: In the model diary entry, why is Ahmed happy at the end of the day?
options: Because he did all his work on time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because he did all his work on time. The model ends: 'I am very happy today because I did all my work on time.' Like Shahban, Ahmed divides his day between prayers, school, homework and helping his father.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Developing a Weekly Timetable
lessons.notes_html:
Developing a Weekly Timetable

Developing a weekly time table is a good habit. It helps you to plan your time properly and helps you remember all the important things that you have to do on any given day.

How to Make It

  • Draw a time table in your notebook with days of the week: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
  • Make four columns: Morning, Afternoon, Evening, Night.
  • Write down two to three things that you will do in the morning, afternoon, evening and at night, for each day of the week.

Model

  • Sunday: Morning — wake up early, exercise. Afternoon — lunch, homework. Evening — play with friends. Night — read a book, sleep early.
  • Monday: Morning — go to school. Afternoon — lunch, homework. Evening — Quran class. Night — TV, sleep.

Self-Created Cloze

Remember to do the Cloze activity as shown in Unit 1, section 1.5 — one paragraph every day in a separate notebook.

mcqs.q: Developing a weekly timetable is a good habit because it ______.
options: helps us plan our time properly and remember all the important things
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it helps us plan our time properly and remember all the important things. This is the book's own opening line of section 4.5. A timetable divides the day between study, work, play and rest — like Shahban's day.

mcqs.q: How many things should we write for each part of the day in the timetable?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: two to three things. The book says, 'Write down two to three things that you will do in the morning, afternoon, evening and at night, for each day in the week.'

mcqs.q: The four columns of the weekly timetable are ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Morning, Afternoon, Evening, Night. The rows are the seven days of the week, from Sunday to Saturday, and each cell holds the work of that part of the day.

mcqs.q: In the model timetable, what is written for Monday evening?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Quran class. The model says: 'Monday: Morning — go to school. Afternoon — lunch, homework. Evening — Quran class. Night — TV, sleep.'

mcqs.q: In the model, Sunday night is for ______.
options: reading a book and sleeping early
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: reading a book and sleeping early. The model Sunday is: Morning — wake up early, exercise; Night — read a book, sleep early. Sleeping early keeps us fresh for the next day.

mcqs.q: A weekly timetable has rows for ______.
options: the seven days of the week
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the seven days of the week. The book lists them: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday. Weekends are planned too, not only school days.

mcqs.q: Section 4.5 also reminds us to do which daily activity?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the Self-Created Cloze of Unit 1.5. The study skills note says, 'Remember to do the Cloze activity as shown in Unit 1.5.' We choose a paragraph, mark every 8th word, and fill the blanks after half an hour.

mcqs.q: Shahban's day in the reading text is a good example of ______.
options: a well-planned day divided between study, work and play
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a well-planned day divided between study, work and play. Shahban studies in the morning, helps at home, attends Quran class, works for two hours, and still has Sundays for play. A timetable helps us do the same.

mcqs.q: Where do we draw the weekly timetable?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in our notebook. The book says, 'Draw a time table, as given below, in your notebook.' We can look at it every day and follow it.

mcqs.q: Which of these belongs in a good daily plan, according to this unit?
options: Doing homework, playing, and sleeping on time
Sleeping till late in the morning
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: doing homework, playing, and sleeping on time. Both the model timetable and Shahban's diary show a balance: school and homework, some play, helping at home, and early sleep.

lessons.title: Fun: I.Q. Game — Spot the Difference
lessons.notes_html:
I.Q. Game — Spot the Difference

In this game there are two pictures that look almost the same — but they are not the same! Work in groups of three and find at least 10 differences in the two pictures.

How to Play

  • Look at both pictures very carefully, part by part.
  • When you find one difference, draw a line from that point in the picture and write number 1.
  • When you find the second difference, write number 2 in the same manner.
  • Continue like this until you find at least 10 differences.
  • Differences can be in the number of trees, colours, clothes, objects, etc.
  • Once you have completed the task, share your findings with another group.
  • Remember: you have to speak in English throughout the activity.

Why This Game Is Useful

This game makes our eyes sharp and our observation strong. We practise speaking English while we point out each difference: 'In picture 1 there are three trees, but in picture 2 there are two trees.'

mcqs.q: In the I.Q. Game, students look at ______.
options: two pictures and find differences between them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: two pictures and find the differences between them. The book says, 'There are some differences in the two pictures given below.' The pictures look alike but have small changes.

mcqs.q: At least how many differences must a group find?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ten. The instruction says: 'Work in groups of three and find at least 10 differences in these two pictures.' Careful looking is needed to find them all.

mcqs.q: How many students work in one group for this game?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three. Like most activities in this book, the I.Q. Game is done 'in groups of three', so students can discuss each difference together.

mcqs.q: When we find a difference, what do we do?
options: We draw a line from that point in the picture and write its number
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: draw a line from that point and write its number. The book says: 'When you find one difference draw a line from that point in the picture and write number 1... When you find the second difference write number 2 in the same manner.'

mcqs.q: In which language must students speak during this activity?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is English. The book reminds us: 'Remember you have to speak in English throughout the activity.' Speaking English about the pictures is part of the learning.

mcqs.q: After completing the task, a group shares its findings with ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: another group. 'Once you have completed the task, share your findings with another group.' Groups can then check whether they found the same differences.

mcqs.q: Which of these can be a difference between the two pictures?
options: The number of trees, colours, clothes or objects
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the number of trees, colours, clothes or objects. The solved answer gives these examples of what to look for: 'number of trees, colours, clothes, objects, etc.'

mcqs.q: This game is called an I.Q. Game because it makes our ______ sharp.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: observation and thinking. Finding small differences between two similar pictures needs sharp eyes and careful thinking, which is why it is placed in the Fun section as an I.Q. game.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct way to report a difference in English?
options: 'In picture 1 there are three trees, but in picture 2 there are two trees.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the second sentence. The notes give this model: we name the picture, say what is there, and use 'but' (the cohesive device of Unit 3) to show the difference in the other picture.

mcqs.q: Why are the differences numbered 1, 2, 3...?
options: To keep count and show each difference clearly
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to keep count and show each difference clearly. Numbering helps the group reach at least 10 differences and helps the other group check them one by one.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Ana, Kofi and Angkul — Children of Three Countries
lessons.notes_html:
Three Children, Three Countries

Ana — Brazil (Text 1). 'Ola!' Ana is 9 years old. She lives in Betim, a city in Brazil, in the continent of South America. The national language of Brazil is Portuguese. Betim is famous for making cars; the largest FIAT car factory is in Betim. Ana has five brothers and two sisters. They do not go to school, but their parents teach them at home. Brazilians celebrate Brasil Sabor from May 3 to June 3 — the world's largest food festival, with more than 2000 types of dishes. Ana's favourite food is Cabidela, cooked with rice and meat. Her hobby is playing with dolls.

Kofi — Ghana (Text 2). 'Sannu!' Kofi means 'Friday'. Kofi is 10 years old and studies in Grade 5 at the School for Deaf and Dumb Heroes. He cannot talk because he was born that way, but he is quite good at catching fish. He lives in Tema, in southeast Ghana, Africa. Tema is the busiest port in Ghana; it used to be a small fishing village and its port was built in 1960. Ghana's main export is cacao. The Ghanans celebrate the Bakatue Festival, on the first Tuesday of July every year, for a good fishing year ahead; once the festival begins, the fishing season starts. Kofi's favourite food is Waakye, cooked with rice and beans.

Angkul — Thailand (Text 3). 'Sawatdee Kaa!' Angkul is 10 years old and studies in Grade 6 in a local public school, where they sit on the floor for lessons. She lives in Phuket, Thailand, in Asia. Phuket is famous for its white beaches and is hot and humid throughout the year. Thais celebrate the Songkran Festival as their New Year's Day, from 13 to 15 April every year, with water fights with water guns. It is also the time to visit and pay respects to elders. Angkul's favourite food is Khao phat, made of rice and meat. Her hobby is painting sceneries.

Key Points

  • One item is common in the food of all three children: rice.
  • Greetings: Ana — Ola; Kofi — Sannu; Angkul — Sawatdee Kaa.
  • People: Brazilians, Ghanans, Thais.
  • Word meanings: famous — well known; largest — biggest; favourite — most liked; deaf — one who cannot hear; dumb — one who cannot speak; export — send to another country; begins — starts; public — government-owned; humid — warm and damp.
  • 'It' in the texts refers to: Betim (a city in Brazil), Brasil Sabor (the world's largest food festival), Bakatue Festival (first Tuesday of July), Waakye (cooked with rice and beans), Phuket (famous for white beaches), Songkran Festival (time to pay respects to elders).

mcqs.q: What are the names of the three children in the reading texts?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Ana, Kofi and Angkul. This is the first question of the reading exercise. Ana is from Brazil, Kofi from Ghana, and Angkul from Thailand.

mcqs.q: One item is common in the food of all three children. What is it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is rice. Ana's Cabidela is cooked with rice and meat, Kofi's Waakye with rice and beans, and Angkul's Khao phat is made of rice and meat. Rice joins all three favourite foods.

mcqs.q: Ana lives in Betim, a city in ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Brazil. Ana says, 'I live in Betim. It is a city in Brazil in the continent of South America.' Brazil is in South America, Ghana in Africa, and Thailand in Asia.

mcqs.q: What is Betim famous for?
options: Making cars — the largest FIAT car factory is there
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: making cars. Ana says, 'My city is famous for making cars. The largest FIAT car factory is in Betim.' Phuket is famous for white beaches, and Tema is the famous port.

mcqs.q: Brasil Sabor is ______.
options: the world's largest food festival, celebrated from May 3 to June 3
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the world's largest food festival. Ana tells us Brazilians celebrate Brasil Sabor from May 3 to June 3, and more than 2000 types of dishes are prepared in it.

mcqs.q: Kofi studies at ______.
options: the School for Deaf and Dumb Heroes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the School for Deaf and Dumb Heroes. Kofi says he is 10 years old and studies in Grade 5 there. He cannot talk because he was born that way, but he is quite good at catching fish.

mcqs.q: The name 'Kofi' means ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Friday. Kofi himself tells us: 'I'm Kofi. It means Friday.' Many fishing communities of Ghana do not go to sea on Tuesdays, and their festival is also fixed by the week — the first Tuesday of July.

mcqs.q: The Bakatue Festival is celebrated ______.
options: on the first Tuesday of July every year
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: on the first Tuesday of July every year. The Ghanans celebrate it for a good fishing year ahead, and once the festival begins, the fishing season starts.

mcqs.q: Ghana's main export is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is cacao. Kofi says, 'Ghana's main export is cacao. The port smells of cocoa beans, fish and salt.' Export means to send to another country.

mcqs.q: Angkul lives in Phuket, which is famous for ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: its white beaches. Angkul says, 'I live in Phuket... It is famous for its white beaches.' Phuket is hot and humid throughout the year, even in winter.

mcqs.q: The Songkran Festival is ______.
options: the Thai New Year's Day, from 13 to 15 April, with water fights
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the Thai New Year's Day, from 13 to 15 April, with water fights. Angkul says people go around the streets with water guns for a water fight, and it is also the time to pay respects to elders.

mcqs.q: Angkul's favourite food, Khao phat, is made of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: rice and meat. Angkul says, 'My favourite food is Khao phat. It is made of rice and meat. We add coconut or pineapple for more taste.' Kofi's Waakye is the food made of rice and beans.

mcqs.q: Which child paints sceneries as a hobby?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Angkul. She says, 'Once I'm free, I like to paint sceneries.' Ana's hobby is playing with dolls, and Kofi's hobby is catching fish.

mcqs.q: The greeting 'Sannu' is used by ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Kofi of Ghana. The greetings are: Ana — 'Ola' (Brazil), Kofi — 'Sannu' (Ghana), Angkul — 'Sawatdee Kaa' (Thailand). Each text begins with the child's own greeting.

mcqs.q: The word 'humid' means ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: warm and damp. In the vocabulary exercise, 'humid' (text 3) means 'warm and damp', and its opposite is 'cool and dry'. Phuket is hot and humid throughout the year.

lessons.title: Speaking: Taking Different Viewpoints into Account
lessons.notes_html:
Taking Different Viewpoints into Account

Four students — Zaman, Rahul, John and Musa — talk about the weather. Each one gives his own viewpoint, and the others agree or state another viewpoint.

The Dialogue — Key Lines

  • Zaman: The weather is very nice today.
  • Rahul: I think it is very hot.
  • John: And I think it is hot and humid.
  • Musa: I don't like hot and humid weather.
  • Zaman: But if we don't have the hot weather we will not get mangoes.
  • Rahul: I agree with Zaman. Heat is good for many fruits and crops.
  • John: My father says that bacteria also grow fast in heat. That is why many people fall sick.
  • Musa: You are right, John. All seasons have their good and bad points.

Key Points

We give our viewpoint with 'I think...', agree with 'I agree with...' and 'You are right', and respect other viewpoints even when our own idea is different. One dialogue is left blank for each character, so every student thinks of one more dialogue about the weather and says it.

mcqs.q: How many students take part in this dialogue?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is four. The book says, 'Practise the following dialogue in groups of four. One student should be Zaman, the others Rahul, John and Musa.' Each character also has one blank dialogue to complete.

mcqs.q: Who says, 'The weather is very nice today'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Zaman. He opens the dialogue. Then each friend gives a different viewpoint: Rahul says it is very hot, John says it is hot and humid, and Musa says he does not like such weather.

mcqs.q: According to John, what does his father say about heat?
options: Bacteria also grow fast in heat, so many people fall sick
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: bacteria also grow fast in heat, so many people fall sick. John adds this bad point of hot weather to the discussion, while Zaman and Rahul speak of the good point — heat is good for mangoes, fruits and crops.

mcqs.q: According to Zaman, if we don't have hot weather, we will not get ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is mangoes. Zaman says, 'But if we don't have the hot weather we will not get mangoes.' Rahul agrees: 'Heat is good for many fruits and crops.'

mcqs.q: Which sentence shows agreement with another person's viewpoint?
options: I think it is very hot
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'I agree with Zaman.' Rahul says this when he accepts Zaman's viewpoint about heat and mangoes. The section teaches us to take different viewpoints into account before deciding.

mcqs.q: What does Musa say at the end?
options: You are right, John. All seasons have their good and bad points
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'You are right, John. All seasons have their good and bad points.' Musa sums up the whole discussion wisely: every season has both good points and bad points.

mcqs.q: In this speaking activity, one dialogue is left ______ for each character.
options: blank, for the student to think of one more dialogue about the weather
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: blank, for the student to think of one more dialogue. The book says: 'Each one should think of one more dialogue related to the weather and say it; the others can agree or state another view point.'

mcqs.q: A suitable extra dialogue for Zaman (from the model answer) is ______.
options: 'I think winter is the best season'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'I think winter is the best season.' The model completion gives: Zaman — I think winter is the best season; Rahul — I agree, winter is pleasant; John — But in winter we cannot eat mangoes; Musa — You are right, but winter has oranges and dry fruits.

mcqs.q: The phrase 'I think...' is used to ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: give our own viewpoint. Rahul says, 'I think it is very hot,' and John says, 'And I think it is hot and humid.' Each boy's viewpoint is different, and all are listened to.

mcqs.q: What is the main skill of this section?
options: Taking different viewpoints into account and respecting them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: taking different viewpoints into account. The section title itself is 'Speaking: Taking into Account Different View Point'. Good speakers listen to all viewpoints, agree where they can, and add their own politely.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Passive Voice
lessons.notes_html:
Active Voice and Passive Voice

In the Active Voice, the doer of the action comes first: 'Father buys the food.'

In the Passive Voice, the receiver of the action comes first: 'The food is bought by father.'

How to Change Active into Passive (Present Simple)

  • Use is / am / are + the past participle form of the verb.
  • I wash the dishes. → The dishes are washed by me.
  • My sister feeds the cows. → The cows are fed by my sister.
  • Grandmother cleans the kitchen. → The kitchen is cleaned by grandmother.
  • My grandfather takes us to school. → We are taken to school by my grandfather.

Past Participle Forms to Remember

wash–washed, feed–fed, cook–cooked, clean–cleaned, pay–paid, cut–cut, drink–drunk, water–watered, do–done, take–taken, read–read, eat–eaten, drive–driven, teach–taught, help–helped, make–made, win–won, like–liked, polish–polished, blow–blown.

Telling Active from Passive

  • Our servant reads the newspaper. — A (Active)
  • Bread and butter are eaten by Salma. — P (Passive)
  • Teachers help students. — A
  • The tractor is driven by their father. — P
  • I am taught English by my sister. — P

mcqs.q: Change into Passive Voice: 'My uncle cooks the food.'
options: The food was cook by my uncle.
The food cooks by my uncle.
The food is cooked by my uncle.
The uncle is cooked by the food.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'The food is cooked by my uncle.' In the passive we use is/am/are + past participle: is + cooked. The receiver (the food) comes first, and the doer comes after 'by'.

mcqs.q: Change into Passive Voice: 'My father pays the bills.'
options: The bills is paid by my father.
The father is paid by the bills.
The bills are pay by my father.
The bills are paid by my father.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'The bills are paid by my father.' 'Bills' is plural, so we use 'are', and the past participle of pay is 'paid'.

mcqs.q: Change into Passive Voice: 'My brother drinks green tea.'
options: Green tea is drunk by my brother.
Green tea is drank by my brother.
Green tea are drunk by my brother.
My brother is drunk by green tea.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Green tea is drunk by my brother.' The past participle of drink is 'drunk', and 'green tea' is singular, so we use 'is'.

mcqs.q: 'Thatta is liked by many people.' This sentence is in ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Passive Voice. It has the form is + past participle (liked) + by. In the book's exercise it is marked P, while 'Our servant reads the newspaper' is marked A.

mcqs.q: 'Honey bees make honey.' This sentence is in ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Active Voice. The doer (honey bees) comes first and does the action (make). Its passive form is: 'Honey is made by honey bees.'

mcqs.q: Change into Active Voice: 'The clouds are blown away by strong winds.'
options: Strong winds blow away the clouds.
The clouds blow the strong winds.
Strong winds are blown by the clouds.
The winds are blown away by clouds.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Strong winds blow away the clouds.' To change passive into active, we bring the doer (strong winds) to the front and use the simple present form 'blow'.

mcqs.q: Change into Active Voice: 'I am taught English by my sister.'
options: My sister is taught English by me.
I teach English to my sister.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'My sister teaches me English.' The doer is 'my sister'; in the active voice she comes first: My sister teaches me English.

mcqs.q: In the Passive Voice we use the ______ form of the verb.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: past participle form. The book's instruction says, 'Remember to use the past participle form of the verb in the Passive Voice. Use is, am or are, as needed.' For example: washed, fed, cooked, taken, done.

mcqs.q: Change into Passive Voice: 'My aunt waters the plants.'
options: The plants is watered by my aunt.
The plants are watered by my aunt.
The plants are watering by my aunt.
My aunt is watered by the plants.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'The plants are watered by my aunt.' 'Plants' is plural, so we use 'are' + the past participle 'watered'.

mcqs.q: Change into Passive Voice: 'My mother does the laundry.'
options: The laundry is done by my mother.
The laundry is did by my mother.
The laundry are done by my mother.
My mother is done by the laundry.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'The laundry is done by my mother.' The past participle of 'do' is 'done', and 'the laundry' is singular, so we use 'is done'.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Prepositions of Time
lessons.notes_html:
Prepositions of Time — At, In, On

  • at — for clock times and special points of the day: at lunch time, at bedtime, at midnight, at 5 o'clock, at noon, at 8:00 am, at night.
  • in — for parts of the day, months, years and seasons: in the evening, in the morning, in December, in 1998, in the winter holidays.
  • on — for days and dates: on Sundays, on Saturday, on Eid, on December 18, on the 23rd of December, on Christmas Day.

Examples from the Book

  • I have no school on Sundays.
  • My father comes home at lunch time.
  • The children like to go to the park in the evening.
  • Lots of people buy new clothes on Eid.
  • There was a loud noise which woke us up at midnight.
  • I met my husband in 1998.
  • The school is opening on Saturday.

The Moenjodaro Trip (Completed)

'Salma and her brother, Rumi, decided to go to Moenjodaro in the winter holidays. They wanted to go on December 18. At breakfast time they asked their father... He called both of them at 5 o'clock... a train leaves for Moenjodaro at 8:00 am. They could take the train in December... They would reach Moenjodaro at noon. Their father said that they could go on the 23rd of December... and come back on Christmas Day... They would give the good news to their mother at night.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'I have no school ______ Sundays.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'on'. We use 'on' with days of the week: on Sundays, on Saturday. With clock times we use 'at', and with months and years we use 'in'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'My father comes home ______ lunch time.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'at'. 'At' is used for points of the day like lunch time, bedtime, midnight and noon: at lunch time, at bedtime, at midnight.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'The children like to go to the park ______ the evening.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'in'. We use 'in' with parts of the day: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening. (But we say 'at night' — that is an exception to remember.)

mcqs.q: Complete: 'There was a loud noise which woke us up ______ midnight.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'at'. Midnight is a point of time, so we say 'at midnight', just like 'at noon' and 'at 5 o'clock'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'I met my husband ______ 1998.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'in'. Years take 'in': in 1998, in 2015. Months also take 'in': in December. Dates and days take 'on'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'The school is opening ______ Saturday.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'on'. Days of the week take 'on': on Saturday, on Sundays. This is from the book's preposition exercise.

mcqs.q: Complete from the Moenjodaro story: 'A train leaves for Moenjodaro ______ 8:00 am.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'at'. Clock times always take 'at': at 8:00 am, at 5 o'clock. Rumi tells his father the train time with 'at'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'They could go ______ the 23rd of December.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'on'. Full dates take 'on': on the 23rd of December, on December 18, on Christmas Day. Only the month or year alone takes 'in'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Mother always tells us a story ______ bedtime.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'at'. 'Bedtime' is a point of the day like lunch time and midnight, so we say 'at bedtime'. Kamal's mother also tells him stories at bedtime in Unit 2.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Lots of people buy new clothes ______ Eid.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'on'. Festival days are treated like days and dates: on Eid, on Christmas Day. The book's answer is: 'Lots of people buy new clothes on Eid.'

lessons.title: Language Practice: Cohesive Devices and Punctuation — Once, Colon and Commas
lessons.notes_html:
Cohesive Device — Once

Once joins two actions: when the first action is finished, the second one happens.

  • Once you finish your science project, I will let you play with your friends.
  • Once they wash their hands, they will be allowed to eat.
  • Once the team finishes the practice, they can go home.
  • Once you finish your food, all of you will get ice cream.
  • Once he says sorry, he will be forgiven.
  • Once she finishes cooking, she should take some rest.
  • Once the field is ploughed, we can start sowing the seeds.

Punctuation — The Colon (:)

A colon comes before a list, after a complete sentence. We do not put a colon in the middle of a broken sentence.

  • Correct: My brother has many hobbies: collecting coins from different countries, reading story books, growing fruits and vegetables, and painting natural scenes.
  • Correct: The basket contained these items: fruit, biscuits, chocolates and sweets.
  • Correct: I can see many things from here: the old lighthouse, seagulls catching fish, children playing on the beach, and boats in the sea.
  • Correct: In the bag there were the following items: scissors, a hairbrush, some money and her address book.

Adding Colons and Commas

  • Please buy these things from the shop: a litre of milk, a loaf of bread, a packet of salt and a tin of oil.
  • Cut all these fruits and put them in the bowl: a mango, three bananas, an orange, two apples and a guava.
  • The girls decided to buy all the things they would need for Eid: dresses, sandals, purses, bangles, earrings and mehndi.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: 'Once they wash their hands, ______.'
options: we can start sowing the seeds
they will be allowed to eat
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'they will be allowed to eat.' This is the book's matching exercise: washing hands comes before eating. The other endings belong to other 'once' sentences.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Once the field is ploughed, ______.'
options: we can start sowing the seeds
all of you will get ice cream
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'we can start sowing the seeds.' Sowing is done after ploughing a field. 'Once' shows that the second action follows the first one.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Once he says sorry, ______.'
options: they will be allowed to eat
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'he will be forgiven.' Saying sorry is the first action; being forgiven follows it. This pair is from the book's Column A–Column B matching.

mcqs.q: Complete with a suitable ending: 'Once the bell rings, ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'we will go home.' After 'Once...', the result is in the future form (will + verb), as in the book's model: 'Once I pass my exams, I will join English classes.'

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses the colon correctly?
options: The basket contained: fruit, biscuits, chocolates and sweets.
The basket contained these items: fruit, biscuits, chocolates and sweets.
The basket: contained fruit, biscuits, chocolates and sweets.
The basket contained these items fruit: biscuits and sweets.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the second sentence. A colon comes after a complete sentence ('The basket contained these items') and before the list. We never break a sentence with a colon, as in 'The basket contained: ...'

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses the colon correctly?
options: My brother has: many hobbies collecting coins, reading story books and painting.
My brother has many: hobbies collecting coins and reading story books.
My brother has many hobbies: collecting coins from different countries, reading story books, growing fruits and vegetables, and painting natural scenes.
My brother: has many hobbies collecting coins and reading.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the third sentence. The part before the colon is a complete sentence — 'My brother has many hobbies' — and the list follows the colon. The other sentences break the sentence in the wrong place.

mcqs.q: Add the colon and commas: 'Please buy these things from the shop a litre of milk a loaf of bread a packet of salt and a tin of oil.'
options: Please buy these things from the shop: a litre of milk, a loaf of bread, a packet of salt and a tin of oil.
Please buy: these things from the shop a litre of milk, a loaf of bread, a packet of salt and a tin of oil.
Please buy these things from the shop a litre of milk, a loaf of bread, a packet of salt, and a tin of oil:
Please: buy these things from the shop: a litre of milk a loaf of bread a packet of salt and a tin of oil.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the first sentence. The colon comes after 'shop', and commas separate the items of the shopping list, with 'and' before the last item.

mcqs.q: Add the colon and commas: 'Cut all these fruits and put them in the bowl a mango three bananas an orange two apples and a guava.'
options: Cut all these fruits and put them in the bowl: a mango, three bananas, an orange, two apples and a guava.
Cut all these fruits: and put them in the bowl a mango three bananas, an orange two apples and a guava.
Cut all these fruits and put them in the bowl a mango: three bananas an orange, two apples and a guava.
Cut: all these fruits and put them in the bowl: a mango three bananas an orange two apples and a guava.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the first sentence. The list of fruits follows the colon, and each fruit is separated by a comma. This is the book's own solved punctuation exercise.

mcqs.q: A colon is used ______.
options: at the end of every sentence
before a list, after a complete sentence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: before a list, after a complete sentence. All the correct examples in the book follow this rule: 'There are many types of trees here: the old neem tree, the mango tree...'

mcqs.q: 'Once you finish your science project, I will let you play with your friends.' Here 'Once' means ______.
options: as soon as / after you finish
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: as soon as / after you finish. This is the book's worked example of the cohesive device 'once' — the second action (playing with friends) happens after the first action (finishing the project) is complete.

lessons.title: Writing: Autobiography — About Myself
lessons.notes_html:
Autobiography — Writing About Myself

An autobiography is the story of our own life, written by ourselves. In this lesson we fill a table about ourselves, on the same pattern as the table of Ana, Kofi and Angkul in section 5.1, and then write 3–4 paragraphs.

The Table About Myself

  • 1. Name 2. Age 3. Class 4. City 5. Country 6. Continent 7. People called 8. Greeting 9. Festival 10. Favourite food 11. Food made of 12. Hobby

Model Table

  • Name: Ahmed. Age: 11. Class: Class 6. City: Hyderabad. Country: Pakistan. Continent: Asia. People called: Pakistanis. Greeting: Assalam-o-Alaikum. Festival: Eid. Favourite food: Biryani. Food made of: rice and meat. Hobby: Playing cricket.

Model Paragraphs

'Assalam-o-Alaikum! I am Ahmed. I am 11 years old and study in Class 6. I live in Hyderabad. It is a city in Pakistan, in the continent of Asia. We are called Pakistanis and our greeting is "Assalam-o-Alaikum". We celebrate Eid. My favourite food is Biryani. It is made of rice and meat. Once I am free, I like to play cricket.'

The reading passages of Ana, Kofi and Angkul are our samples: each child writes the greeting first, then name, age, city, country, festival, favourite food and hobby.

mcqs.q: An autobiography is ______.
options: the story of our own life, written by ourselves
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the story of our own life, written by ourselves. In section 5.4 we write about ourselves, just as Ana, Kofi and Angkul wrote about themselves in the reading texts.

mcqs.q: Which table is used as the pattern for writing about ourselves?
options: The table of Ana, Kofi and Angkul in exercise 5, section 5.1
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the table of the three children in section 5.1. The writing exercise says, 'Look at the table in exercise 5, section 5.1. Based on the same pattern, fill the following table about yourself.'

mcqs.q: How many pieces of information are there in the table about myself?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is twelve. They are: name, age, class, city, country, continent, people called, greeting, festival, favourite food, food made of, and hobby — exactly like the table of the three children.

mcqs.q: In the model, Ahmed's greeting is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Assalam-o-Alaikum. Ahmed is a Pakistani child, so his greeting is 'Assalam-o-Alaikum'. Ola is Ana's greeting, Sannu is Kofi's, and Sawatdee Kaa is Angkul's.

mcqs.q: In the model table, Ahmed's favourite food is Biryani, which is made of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: rice and meat. The model says: 'Favourite food: Biryani. Food made of: rice and meat.' This is the same as Angkul's Khao phat, while Kofi's Waakye is made of rice and beans.

mcqs.q: How many paragraphs do we write about ourselves in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 3–4 paragraphs. The exercise says, 'Using the information in the above table, write 3-4 paragraphs about yourself. Use the reading text passages in section 5.1 as your sample.'

mcqs.q: The model autobiography begins with ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the greeting. Like the three reading passages, the model begins with the child's greeting and name: 'Assalam-o-Alaikum! I am Ahmed. I am 11 years old and study in Class 6.'

mcqs.q: People of Pakistan are called ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Pakistanis. In the model table: 'People called: Pakistanis.' In the reading texts, people of Brazil are Brazilians, of Ghana are Ghanans, and of Thailand are Thais.

mcqs.q: Ahmed lives in Hyderabad, which is in the continent of ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Asia. The model says, 'It is a city in Pakistan, in the continent of Asia.' Thailand is also in Asia, Ghana is in Africa, and Brazil is in South America.

mcqs.q: Ahmed's hobby in the model is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: playing cricket. The model ends: 'Once I am free, I like to play cricket.' Painting sceneries is Angkul's hobby, dolls are Ana's, and catching fish is Kofi's.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Free Writing and Reading Aloud
lessons.notes_html:
Free Writing

Free Writing means: writing without stopping. Doing this activity every day can help you gain confidence in writing. Do it even when you go to Class VII and VIII.

How to Do Free Writing

  • Spend just 5 minutes on this activity every day.
  • Have a separate copy for this work.
  • Choose a topic of your choice: a person, place, thing, idea, like or dislike — a TV programme, a wedding, a festival, or a fight with your brother/sister/friend.
  • Write without stopping, in any order you like. Write whatever is in your mind.
  • Do not worry about the punctuation, spelling, grammar or handwriting.
  • If you cannot think of an English word or phrase, write that word or phrase in any other language, but do not stop writing. Find out the English word later and write it where it should be written.
  • This work is NOT corrected.

Two More Daily Habits

  • Continue practising the Self-Created Cloze (Unit 1.5) on a paragraph of this text or any other text.
  • Do some loud reading every day. Reading aloud develops spoken language. You can also read in pairs: your friend reads one sentence and you read the next.

mcqs.q: Free Writing means ______.
options: writing very fast in an exam
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: writing without stopping. The book defines it in the title line itself: 'Free-writing: Writing without stopping.' We keep the pen moving for the full time.

mcqs.q: How much time do we spend on Free Writing every day?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 5 minutes. Step 1 says, 'Spend just 5 minutes on this activity every day.' It is a short daily activity, like the Self-Created Cloze.

mcqs.q: In Free Writing, if an English word does not come to our mind, we should ______.
options: write that word in any other language and keep writing; find the English word later
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: write the word in another language and keep writing. The rule says: do not stop writing to think about it; however, find out the English word or phrase later and write it down where it should be written.

mcqs.q: In Free Writing, we should NOT worry about ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: punctuation, spelling, grammar or handwriting. The book says clearly, 'Do not worry about the punctuation, spelling, grammar or handwriting.' The aim is confidence and flow of ideas, and this work is not corrected.

mcqs.q: Free Writing is done in ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a separate copy. Step 1 says, 'Have a separate copy for this work.' The Self-Created Cloze also has its own separate notebook.

mcqs.q: Which can be a topic for Free Writing?
options: A TV programme, a wedding, a festival, or a fight with a friend
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a TV programme, a wedding, a festival, or a fight. The book says we can write about anything that is in our mind — a person, place, thing, idea, like or dislike.

mcqs.q: Is Free Writing corrected by the teacher?
options: No, this work is NOT corrected
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: No, this work is NOT corrected. The solved note says it clearly. That is why we can write freely without fear of mistakes.

mcqs.q: Reading aloud every day helps us to develop ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: spoken language. The study skill note says, 'Make sure that you find time to do some loud reading every day. Reading aloud will help you develop spoken language.'

mcqs.q: In pair loud reading, ______.
options: your friend reads one sentence and you read the next
only one friend reads the whole text
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: your friend reads one sentence and you read the next. The book says, 'You can also read the text in pairs. Your friend will read one sentence and you will read the next.'

mcqs.q: Free Writing should be continued ______.
options: even in Class VII and VIII
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: even in Class VII and VIII. The book says, 'Do this activity even when you go to class VII and VIII.' Daily writing practice builds confidence year after year.

lessons.title: Fun: Fun with Verbs
lessons.notes_html:
Fun with Verbs

In this game we sort words into two groups: Present Simple verbs (colour them green) and Past Participle verbs (colour them red). The other words in the table are not verbs at all — they are nouns, adjectives and place names.

Present Simple Verbs (Green)

bring, make, eat, help, feed, pay, clean, cook, drink, teach.

Past Participle Verbs (Red)

liked, polished, taught, washed, done, eaten, taken, blown, won, driven.

Not Verbs

bird, woman, Peshawar, snake, hungry, tree, zebra, insect, zoo, Karachi, happy, easy, zip, smart, child, hair, farm, late, fun, Kohat, uncle, teeth, house, Attock, elephant, star, Pasni, man, angry.

Remember the Pairs

  • eat — eaten; teach — taught; take — taken; do — done
  • blow — blown; win — won; drive — driven; wash — washed
  • like — liked; polish — polished
