These past participle forms are the same forms we used in the Passive Voice lesson: 'The food is cooked', 'We are taken to school', 'Honey is made by honey bees'.

mcqs.q: Which of these words is a Present Simple verb?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'bring'. In the Fun with Verbs table, the Present Simple verbs (green) are: bring, make, eat, help, feed, pay, clean, cook, drink, teach. 'Eaten' is a past participle, 'Karachi' is a place name and 'hungry' is an adjective.

mcqs.q: Which of these words is a Past Participle verb?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'taken'. The past participles (red) are: liked, polished, taught, washed, done, eaten, taken, blown, won, driven. 'Teach' is the present simple form; its past participle is 'taught'.

mcqs.q: The past participle of 'eat' is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'eaten'. In the table, 'eat' is green (present simple) and 'eaten' is red (past participle). We use it in the passive: 'Bread and butter are eaten by Salma.'

mcqs.q: The past participle of 'teach' is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'taught'. The solved table lists 'taught' among the red past participles. Example from the passive lesson: 'I am taught English by my sister.'

mcqs.q: Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: win — won. The other pairs are wrong: do — done, blow — blown, drive — driven. These irregular past participles must be memorised.

mcqs.q: Which word in the table is NOT a verb?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'zebra'. A zebra is an animal — a noun. Feed, pay and clean are all present simple verbs (green). The table also has nouns like bird, snake, tree, house and elephant, and place names like Karachi, Peshawar, Kohat, Attock and Pasni.

mcqs.q: Which word is an adjective in the table?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'happy'. Happy, hungry, angry, easy, smart and late are adjectives in the table. They describe nouns; they are not action words, so they are not coloured green or red.

mcqs.q: In the game, Present Simple verbs are coloured ______ and Past Participle verbs are coloured ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: green for Present Simple and red for Past Participle. The instruction says: 'Colour the Present Simple verbs in green. Colour the Past Participle verbs in red.'

mcqs.q: The past participle of 'drive' is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'driven'. Example from this unit: 'The tractor is driven by their father.' The simple past is 'drove', but the passive voice needs the past participle 'driven'.

mcqs.q: Past participle forms are needed for ______.
options: the Passive Voice — is/am/are + past participle
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the Passive Voice. In section 5.3 we learnt: passive = is/am/are + past participle, e.g. 'The dishes are washed', 'The kitchen is cleaned', 'We are taken to school.' This Fun game helps us remember those forms.

chapters.title: Learning Through Personal Interests, Abilities and Hobbies

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Yes, You Can — An Interview with Mohammed Tahir
lessons.notes_html:
About Mohammed Tahir

Mohammed Tahir is a Sindh Gymnast Champion. He has been a member of the Sindh Sports Board since 1993. He has competed for the Sindh Team of Gymnastics in Hyderabad, Islamabad, Karachi, Lahore, Larkana, Quetta and other cities. He has won many gold, silver and bronze medals, and silver and bronze medals at the 32nd National Games 2013 in Islamabad. He is a sports and gymnastics coach at a local school in Karachi. Tahir wants to be a world champion to make his parents and country proud. This interview was conducted by Munazza Mahmood Alam.

Tahir's Profile

  • Name: Mohammed Tahir
  • Date of Birth: January 1st (year not given)
  • Place of Birth: Karachi
  • Place of Work: A local school in Karachi
  • Hobbies: Reading sports, watching sports, table-tennis
  • Children Coached: More than a thousand

Key Points from the Interview

  • He has been a gymnast since he was 6 years old. His father and brothers are gymnasts; he picked it up as a hobby.
  • Gymnastics has made him a better sportsman, a good teacher and a physically stronger person. His body balance has become good, and he has developed self-control and become very tolerant.
  • His daily routine: gets up early, sleeps early, eats on time, practices every day, jogs daily.
  • To be successful: practice very hard, stick to your goal, and be fair.
  • A good sportsperson needs mental and physical stamina, healthy food, and must keep away from unhealthy habits. Spicy and oily foods are harmful. Smoking weakens the lungs. Paan, chaaliya, tobacco and gutka are dangerous.
  • Gymnastics is healthy; it relaxes stiff muscles and calms stress. It is fun too!
  • Children should start practising gymnastics at about five years of age, but anybody can learn it.
  • A good sportsperson respects his parents, helps whenever and wherever he can, and is never selfish.
  • Tahir's motto: 'Work, play, and work!'

Word Meanings

gymnast — the person who practises gymnastics; gymnastics — a sport which involves moving the body in particular ways; hobby — interest in doing something; self-control — keeping oneself in control; coach — the person who trains players; tolerant — bearing or being patient in spite of feeling pain; routine — a daily programme of tasks; stamina — the ability to stay active for a long time; talent — something that you can naturally do well; relaxes — to reduce tension or worry; stiff — not moving; calms — to make someone calm; stress — tension or worry; flexible — easy to bend or fold.

mcqs.q: Who is Mohammed Tahir?
options: The Sindh Gymnast Champion and a coach at a local school in Karachi
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the Sindh Gymnast Champion and a coach in Karachi. The introduction says he has been a member of the Sindh Sports Board since 1993 and has won many gold, silver and bronze medals.

mcqs.q: Where and when was Tahir born?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in Karachi, on January 1st. In the interview's first dialogue, Tahir says, 'I was born on January 1st in Karachi.' The year is not given in the text.

mcqs.q: Since what age has Tahir been a gymnast?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: six years old. Tahir says, 'I have been a gymnast since I was 6 years old.' He advises that children should start at about five years of age, when their bones are soft and flexible.

mcqs.q: How did Tahir get into gymnastics?
options: His father and brothers were gymnasts; he picked it up as a hobby
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: his father and brothers were gymnasts, and he picked it up as a hobby. This is Tahir's own answer in dialogue 3 of the interview.

mcqs.q: How many children has Tahir coached in gymnastics?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: more than a thousand. Tahir says, 'I have coached more than a thousand children in gymnastics.' The true/false exercise warns us not to say 'one lakh' — that statement is false.

mcqs.q: The word 'gymnastics' is said ______ times by the interviewer and ______ times by Tahir.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 4 times by the interviewer and 2 times by Tahir. This is Exercise 1 of the reading section: the interviewer says it in Questions 3, 5, 9 and 10, and Tahir says it in 'I coach children in gymnastics' and 'Gymnastics is a sport'.

mcqs.q: What is Tahir's daily routine?
options: Gets up late, eats late, rests all day
Gets up early, sleeps early, eats on time, practices every day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: gets up early, sleeps early, eats on time and practices every day. Tahir says, 'I follow a strict routine. I get up early and sleep early. I eat on time and practice every day. I keep fit. I jog daily.'

mcqs.q: According to Tahir, to be successful in any sport we must ______.
options: practice very hard, stick to our goal, and be fair
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: practice very hard, stick to our goal, and be fair. Tahir says, 'If you want to be successful in any sports, you have to practice very hard, stick to your goal, and be fair!'

mcqs.q: Which foods are harmful for sportspersons?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: spicy and oily foods. Tahir says, 'If you eat healthy food, you will be fit. Spicy and oily foods are harmful.' He also warns against smoking, paan, chaaliya, tobacco and gutka.

mcqs.q: What does smoking do, according to Tahir?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it weakens the lungs. Tahir says, 'If you smoke, your lungs will become weak.' That is why a good sportsperson keeps away from unhealthy habits.

mcqs.q: How is gymnastics good for us?
options: It is healthy, relaxes stiff muscles and calms stress — and it is fun too
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it is healthy, relaxes stiff muscles and calms stress, and it is fun too. This is Tahir's answer in dialogue 9. The statement 'Gymnastics is only hard work and no fun' is false.

mcqs.q: At what age should children start practising gymnastics?
options: At about five years of age
Only small children can learn it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: at about five years of age. Tahir says it is easier for children because their bones are soft and flexible, 'It is best to start when a child is about five years old.' But anybody can take up gymnastics — 'Why not!'.

mcqs.q: What is the meaning of 'stamina'?
options: The ability which allows someone to stay active for a long time
Something you can naturally do well
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the ability to stay active for a long time. A good sportsperson needs mental and physical stamina. 'Routine' means a daily programme of tasks, 'self-control' means keeping oneself in control, and 'talent' means something you can naturally do well.

mcqs.q: What is Tahir's motto?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Work, play, and work!' This is the last line of Tahir's message to the children of Pakistan: 'All in all, work, play, and work! The path to success will become very easy!'

mcqs.q: What message does Tahir give to the children of Pakistan?
options: Have faith in Allah, respect your parents, help others and never be selfish
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: have faith in Allah, respect your parents, help whenever and wherever you can, and never be selfish. He also advises a daily and weekly timetable and a healthy, positive sport.

lessons.title: Speaking: Expressing Ability and Inability
lessons.notes_html:
Expressing Ability and Inability

In this section we talk about the things we can do and the things we cannot do, and about teaching each other new things.

The Dialogue — Najma and Zainab

  • Najma: Do you know what pattern Baji is going to teach us to stitch?
  • Zainab: No. Do you know?
  • Najma: No, I don't know. I hope the work is not going to be difficult.
  • Zainab: Stitching clothes is very interesting. I remember when we were small, we used to learn flowers on clothes. Now we need to work on big clothes.
  • Najma: What kind of clothes are we going to stitch?
  • Zainab: I don't know. But it depends on what pattern Baji gives us.

Group Discussion — Who Can Do What?

  • Which of us can do what things?
  • What things can you teach somebody?
  • If the members of the group teach each other, can they learn to do these things?

Model discussion: 'I can play cricket and teach my friends. I can ride a bicycle. My friend knows stitching and she can teach me. If we teach each other, we can learn new things.'

Talking About Our Favourite Game

We also tell which game we like and write 5 things we like about it. Model: 'I like cricket. 1. It is a team game. 2. It keeps me healthy and active. 3. It teaches me teamwork. 4. It is fun. 5. I can play with my friends.'

mcqs.q: The speaking section 6.2 is about expressing ______.
options: ability and inability to do something
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: ability and inability to do something. The Contents page names section 6.2 'Speaking: Expressing Ability and Inability to do something'. We use 'can' for ability and 'cannot' for inability.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, what is Baji going to teach Najma and Zainab?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a pattern to stitch. Najma asks, 'Do you know what pattern Baji is going to teach us to stitch?' Neither girl knows the pattern yet.

mcqs.q: What did the girls use to learn when they were small?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: flowers on clothes. Zainab says, 'I remember when we were small, we used to learn flowers on clothes. Now we need to work on big clothes.' Their stitching work is growing with them.

mcqs.q: According to Zainab, stitching clothes is ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: very interesting. Zainab says, 'Stitching clothes is very interesting.' Najma only hopes the new work is not going to be difficult.

mcqs.q: The kind of clothes the girls will stitch depends on ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: what pattern Baji gives them. Zainab's last line is: 'I don't know. But it depends on what pattern Baji gives us.'

mcqs.q: Which sentence expresses ABILITY?
options: I can play cricket and teach my friends
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'I can play cricket and teach my friends.' 'Can' shows ability. This sentence is from the model group discussion of this section.

mcqs.q: Which sentence expresses INABILITY?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'I cannot do this work.' 'Cannot' (can't) shows inability — a thing we are not able to do. The other sentences use 'can' and show ability.

mcqs.q: What is the main question of the group discussion?
options: Which of us can do what things, and what things can you teach somebody?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: which of us can do what things, and what things can you teach somebody. The group then discusses: if the members teach each other, can they learn to do these things? The model answer says yes.

mcqs.q: According to the model discussion, if group members teach each other, they ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: can learn new things. The model says: 'My friend knows stitching and she can teach me. If we teach each other, we can learn new things.' Sharing abilities helps everyone.

mcqs.q: In the model answer about a favourite game, how many things are written about cricket?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is five. The speaking task says, 'Which game do you like? Write 5 things you like about it.' The model writes five things about cricket: it is a team game, keeps us healthy and active, teaches teamwork, is fun, and can be played with friends.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Wh-Question Words
lessons.notes_html:
Wh-Question Words

  • What — to ask about a thing: What is your name?
  • Who — to ask about a person: Who did you talk to at school?
  • Whose — to ask about the owner: Whose bag is this?
  • When — to ask about time: When do you think you will come back?
  • Where — to ask about a place: Where do you live?
  • Why — to ask about a reason: Why do you like cricket?
  • How — to ask the way: How did you reach home?
  • How many — to ask about number: How many mangoes are there in the basket?
  • How much — to ask about price or quantity: How much did you buy this for?
  • How often — to ask how many times: How often do you go to school?
  • How far — to ask about distance: How far was the airport?
  • What time — What time did the drama serial begin?
  • Which — to ask about a choice: Which book is more interesting?

Making Questions for Answers

  • Answer: I returned from Quetta on Monday. → When did you return from Quetta?
  • Answer: The airport was 5 km away. → How far was the airport?
  • Answer: This is Sara's bag. → Whose bag is this?
  • Answer: My aunt lives in Karachi. → Where does your aunt live?
  • Answer: My favourite fruit is mango. → What is your favourite fruit?

mcqs.q: Complete the question: '______ did you talk to at school?'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Who'. We ask about a person with 'Who'. The book's answers are: 2) Who, 3) How, 4) When, 5) Where, 6) What, 7) How much, 8) How often, 9) Whose, 10) How many.

mcqs.q: Complete: '______ do you live?'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Where'. We ask about a place with 'Where': 'Where do you live?' — 'I live in Hyderabad.'

mcqs.q: Complete: '______ bag is this?'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Whose'. 'Whose' asks about the owner of a thing: 'Whose bag is this?' — 'This is Sara's bag.'

mcqs.q: Complete: '______ mangoes are there in the basket?'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How many'. Mangoes can be counted, so we ask 'How many'. 'How much' is used for price or uncountable quantities.

mcqs.q: Make a question for this answer: 'I returned from Quetta on Monday.'
options: When did you return from Quetta?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'When did you return from Quetta?' The answer tells the time (on Monday), so the question word must be 'When'. Making the question match the answer is the skill of this exercise.

mcqs.q: Make a question for this answer: 'The airport was 5 km away.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'How far was the airport?' The answer gives a distance (5 km), and distance is asked with 'How far'.

mcqs.q: Make a question for this answer: 'My aunt lives in Karachi.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Where does your aunt live?' The answer names a place (Karachi), so we ask with 'Where'.

mcqs.q: Make a question for this answer: 'Your father is knocking on the door.'
options: What is knocking on the door?
Who is knocking on the door?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'Who is knocking on the door?' The answer names a person (your father), so the question word is 'Who'.

mcqs.q: Complete: '______ do you go to school — by bus or on foot?' (way/manner)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'How'. The book's model answers give: 'How do you come to school? — I come by bus.' 'How' asks about the way or manner of doing something, and the answer here is about travelling by bus or on foot.

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about a reason?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Why'. Example from the model answers: 'Why do you like cricket? — Because it is fun.' A 'Why' question is answered with 'because'.

lessons.title: Language Practice: First Conditional
lessons.notes_html:
First Conditional

We use the First Conditional to talk about a possible future action and its result.

Form: If + present simple, ... will + verb.

  • If you stay up late, you will be tired in the morning.
  • If he comes, I will be surprised.
  • If we go on holiday this summer, we will go to China.
  • If the weather does not improve, we will not have a picnic.
  • They will go to the party if they are invited.

Matching Conditions and Results

  • If we don't throw trash in the seas and rivers, the earth will be a better place.
  • If you eat too much chocolate, you will get fat.
  • If people don't throw rubbish on the roads, the roads can be clean.
  • If we go to bed late, we cannot wake up early.
  • If my mother tells me a story, I will sleep better.
  • If people don't cut trees, fish will not die.
  • If my father stops eating tobacco, he will get better soon.

Writing Our Own Results

  • If Tasneem has a free train ticket, she will go to Lahore.
  • If they give him a gift, he will be happy.
  • If it is hot this evening, we will go to the park.
  • If we arrive early, the bus will leave on time.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'If you stay up late, you ______ tired in the morning.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'will be'. This is the book's given example of the First Conditional: If + present simple (stay), will + verb (will be). The result is in the future.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'If he comes, I ______ surprised.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'will be'. The model answer is: 'If he comes, I will be surprised.' After an 'if' clause in the present simple, the result clause uses 'will'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Anwar will be late if he ______ here longer.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'waits'. In the 'if' part of the First Conditional we use the present simple: 'if he waits'. We do not use 'will' inside the if-clause.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'If the weather does not improve, we ______ have a picnic.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'will not'. The model answer is: 'If the weather does not improve, we will not have a picnic.' The negative result uses 'will not' (won't).

mcqs.q: Match the correct result: 'If you eat too much chocolate, ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'you will get fat.' This is the book's matching exercise. Eating too much chocolate makes a person fat — condition and result must make sense together.

mcqs.q: Match the correct result: 'If people don't cut trees, ______.'
options: the earth will be a better place in the sea only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'fish will not die.' This is the book's own matching for item 9: 'If people don't cut trees, fish will not die.' Cutting trees harms nature and the waters where fish live, so the two clauses belong together.

mcqs.q: Match the correct result: 'If we go to bed late, ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'we cannot wake up early.' The book's matching gives: 'If we go to bed late, we cannot wake up early.' Late sleeping makes early rising impossible.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is a correct First Conditional sentence?
options: If I will see a snake, I kill it.
If I see a snake near me, I will kill it.
If I saw a snake, I will kill it yesterday.
If I see a snake, I killed it.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'If I see a snake near me, I will kill it.' This is the book's given example: present simple in the if-clause (see), and will + verb in the result clause (will kill).

mcqs.q: Complete: 'If Tasneem has a free train ticket, she ______ to Lahore.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'will go'. The model answer is: 'If Tasneem has a free train ticket, she will go to Lahore.' The if-clause is present simple (has), so the result uses 'will go'.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'They will go to the party if they ______ invited.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'are'. The model answer is: 'They will go to the party if they are invited.' Even when the if-clause comes second, it stays in the present simple — 'are invited', not 'will be invited'.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Cohesive Devices — As and Because
lessons.notes_html:
Cohesive Devices — As and Because

Because gives the reason for something. It usually comes in the middle of the sentence.

  • Saeed is going to the bicycle mechanic's because his bicycle is broken.
  • Jaleel was soaked from head to toe because he walked in the rain from school.
  • I got sick because the fruit was not washed properly.
  • We served biryani for dinner because it was my sister's wedding.

As also gives a reason. It often comes at the beginning of the sentence.

  • As it was a hot summer day, we all decided to have cold lassi.
  • As I have a beautiful garden, many people come to admire it.
  • As the fruit was not washed properly, I got sick when I ate it.

Events and Reasons (from the Book)

  • Saeed is going to the bicycle mechanic's. — His bicycle is broken.
  • Daud would like to buy a new watch. — His old one fell in the river.
  • Mother did not cook last night. — She was looking after the baby.
  • Hajrah slipped and fell down. — There was a banana peel on the floor.
  • Many people come to admire my garden. — I have a beautiful garden.

Making Our Own Sentences

Model: 'I want to learn English because it is an international language. I want to learn English as it will help me in my studies. I want to learn English because I want to read English books.'

mcqs.q: Why is Saeed going to the bicycle mechanic's?
options: Because he wants a new bicycle
Because it is a hot day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because his bicycle is broken. This is the book's worked example of matching events with reasons: 'Saeed is going to the bicycle mechanic's — d. His bicycle is broken.'

mcqs.q: Jaleel was soaked from head to toe because ______.
options: he was playing with water guns
he walked in the rain from school
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: he walked in the rain from school. 'Soaked from head to toe' means completely wet, and the reason given in the book is that he walked home in the rain.

mcqs.q: Why would Daud like to buy a new watch?
options: His old one fell in the river
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: his old one fell in the river. The event-reason matching pairs Daud's new watch with the reason 'His old one fell in the river', so he needs a new watch.

mcqs.q: Why did Mother not cook last night?
options: She was looking after the baby
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: she was looking after the baby. This is reason (a) in the book's matching exercise for the event 'Mother did not cook last night.'

mcqs.q: Why did Hajrah slip and fall down?
options: The floor was wet with water
There was a banana peel on the floor
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: there was a banana peel on the floor. The book pairs the event 'Hajrah slipped and fell down' with this reason. Banana peels are slippery, so we should not throw them on paths.

mcqs.q: Complete with 'as': '______ it was a hot summer day, we all decided to have cold lassi.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'As'. When the reason comes at the beginning of the sentence, we use 'As': 'As it was a hot summer day, we all decided to have cold lassi.' This is the book's own rewritten sentence.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: I want to learn English because it is an international language.
I want to learn English because it is a international language only for exams.
I want to learn English as because it is international.
Because I want to learn English it is an international language.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the first sentence. It is the book's model sentence: 'I want to learn English because it is an international language.' 'Because' joins the action with its reason in the middle of the sentence.

mcqs.q: Why did the speaker get sick?
options: Because he ate too much chocolate
Because the fruit was not washed properly
Because he walked in the rain
Because it was a hot day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because the fruit was not washed properly. The book gives both forms: 'I got sick because the fruit was not washed properly' and 'As the fruit was not washed properly, I got sick when I ate it.'

mcqs.q: Why did the family serve biryani for dinner?
options: Because guests were coming from Brazil
Because it was my sister's wedding
Because it was a hot summer day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because it was my sister's wedding. The event 'We served biryani for dinner' is matched with the reason 'It was my sister's wedding' — biryani is a special dish for a special day.

mcqs.q: Why do many people come to admire the speaker's garden?
options: Because the garden is very big
Because I have a beautiful garden
Because the garden has a swing
Because it is free to enter
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: because I have a beautiful garden. The book also rewrites it with 'as': 'As I have a beautiful garden, many people come to admire it.' Both 'as' and 'because' give reasons.

lessons.title: Writing: Writing an Interview
lessons.notes_html:
Writing an Interview

An interview is a set of questions we ask a person to learn about his or her life, work, interests and hobbies. In this lesson we interview our class fellow.

Step 1 — Write the Questions

  • What is your name?
  • How old are you?
  • Who are your parents?
  • Where do you live?
  • What are your interests?
  • What are your hobbies?
  • Which game do you like?

Step 2 — Fill the Form

  • Model form: Name: Ali. Age: 11. Parents: Muhammad and Fatima. Lives in: Hyderabad. Interests: Reading, cricket. Hobbies: Painting, cycling. Favourite game: Cricket.

Step 3 — Write Four Paragraphs

  • Paragraph 1: Personal information.
  • Paragraph 2: Education.
  • Paragraph 3: Habits.
  • Paragraph 4: Favourites, likes and dislikes.

Model: '1) My class fellow is Ali. He is 11 years old and lives in Hyderabad. His parents are Muhammad and Fatima. 2) He studies in Class 6. He likes English and Science. 3) He gets up early and goes to school every day. He does his homework on time. 4) His favourite game is cricket. He likes reading and he does not like dirty mud.'

Our guide is the interview of Mohammed Tahir in section 6.1: the interviewer asks questions, and the answers give us the person's profile.

mcqs.q: What is an interview?
options: A set of questions we ask a person to learn about him or her
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a set of questions we ask a person to learn about him or her. In section 6.1, Munazza Mahmood Alam interviews Mohammed Tahir; in this lesson we interview our own class fellow in the same way.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct interview question for the form?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'What is your name?' The book says: 'First write your questions for the interview, then ask your class fellow the questions.' The model questions are all Wh-questions like the ones in section 6.3.

mcqs.q: In the model form, where does Ali live?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hyderabad. The model interview form says: 'Name: Ali. Age: 11. Parents: Muhammad and Fatima. Lives in: Hyderabad. Interests: Reading, cricket. Hobbies: Painting, cycling. Favourite game: Cricket.'

mcqs.q: What are Ali's hobbies in the model form?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: painting and cycling. Reading and cricket are written under 'Interests' in the model form, while 'Hobbies' are painting and cycling. His favourite game is cricket.

mcqs.q: How many paragraphs do we write about our class fellow?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is four. The writing exercise says: 'Using the information in the above form, write four paragraphs about your class fellow' — personal information, education, habits, and favourites, likes and dislikes.

mcqs.q: Paragraph 2 of the interview writing is about ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: education. The plan is: Paragraph 1 — personal information; Paragraph 2 — education; Paragraph 3 — habits; Paragraph 4 — favourites, likes and dislikes. In the model, paragraph 2 tells Ali's class and favourite subjects.

mcqs.q: Paragraph 3 is about the class fellow's ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: habits. In the model, paragraph 3 says: 'He gets up early and goes to school every day. He does his homework on time.' Habits are the things a person does regularly.

mcqs.q: Before asking the questions, we should ______.
options: first write our questions for the interview
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: first write our questions for the interview. The book's order is: 'First write your questions for the interview, then ask your class fellow the questions.' Prepared questions make a good interview, like Tahir's interview in 6.1.

mcqs.q: Who conducted the interview of Mohammed Tahir in section 6.1?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Munazza Mahmood Alam. The reading text ends its introduction with: 'This interview was conducted by Munazza Mahmood Alam.' Her questions are our model for writing interview questions.

mcqs.q: In the model paragraph 1, Ali's parents are ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Muhammad and Fatima. Both the model form and the model paragraph 1 give these names: 'His parents are Muhammad and Fatima.' Paragraph 1 carries the personal information from the form.

lessons.title: Study Skills: My Priorities, Cloze and Free Writing
lessons.notes_html:
My Priorities — What Is Most Important in School?

Our teacher has selected these aims of school. We rank them in order of importance according to our own opinion:

  • to know about the world
  • to meet other young people
  • to know about what is good and bad
  • to learn different subjects
  • to find out what I am interested in
  • to test my smartness
  • to learn how to work with books
  • to have a good time
  • to learn discipline
  • to make my parents proud

Model ranking (personal opinion): 1. To know about the world. 2. To learn different subjects. 3. To know about what is good and bad. 4. To make my parents proud. 5. To learn discipline. 6. To find out what I am interested in. 7. To test my smartness. 8. To learn how to work with books. 9. To meet other young people. 10. To have a good time.

Daily Study Habits of This Book

  • Continue practising the Self-Created Cloze (Unit 1.5) on a paragraph of this text or any other text.
  • Continue Free Writing: 5 minutes daily, in a separate copy, without stopping.

mcqs.q: In 'My Priorities', students rank the aims of school ______.
options: in order of importance according to their own opinion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in order of importance according to their own opinion. The exercise says, 'Rank these aims in order of importance according to your opinion.' Different students may rank them differently.

mcqs.q: How many aims are given in the list?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ten. The list is: know about the world, meet other young people, know good and bad, learn different subjects, find out my interests, test my smartness, learn to work with books, have a good time, learn discipline, make my parents proud.

mcqs.q: In the model ranking, which aim is number 1?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to know about the world. The model ranking begins: '1. To know about the world. 2. To learn different subjects. 3. To know about what is good and bad. 4. To make my parents proud...' It is a personal opinion, so your own ranking can differ.

mcqs.q: Which aim is about knowing right from wrong?
options: To know about what is good and bad
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to know about what is good and bad. It stands at number 3 in the model ranking. School teaches us values along with subjects.

mcqs.q: In the model ranking, 'to make my parents proud' is at number ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 4. The model order is: 1 world, 2 subjects, 3 good and bad, 4 make my parents proud, 5 learn discipline, 6 find out my interests, 7 test my smartness, 8 work with books, 9 meet young people, 10 have a good time.

mcqs.q: Which two study activities does this section ask us to continue?
options: Spot the difference and word search
Writing a diary and a newspaper
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Self-Created Cloze and Free Writing. Section 6.5 ends with: 'Continue practicing the Self-created Cloze... Refer to Unit 1.5 for guidance' and 'Continue Free Writing.' Both are daily habits from this book.

mcqs.q: Free Writing is done for ______ minutes daily.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 5 minutes. This rule is from Unit 5, section 5.5: 'Spend just 5 minutes on this activity every day... Write without stopping.' Section 6.5 asks us to continue it.

mcqs.q: In Self-Created Cloze, the paragraph we copy comes from ______.
options: one of the paragraphs of this text or any other text
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a paragraph of this text or any other text. Section 6.5 says: 'Continue practicing the Self-created Cloze on one of the paragraphs of this text or on any other text. Refer to Unit 1.5 for guidance.'

mcqs.q: 'To learn discipline' means ______.
options: to learn to behave well and follow rules in an orderly way
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to learn to behave well and follow rules in an orderly way. Discipline is one of the ten aims of school in this list; Shahban's planned day in Unit 4 is a good example of a disciplined life.

mcqs.q: Why do we rank our priorities?
options: To know what is most important for us in school and work for it first
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: to know what is most important for us and work for it first. 'Priorities' means the things that come first. Knowing our priorities helps us use our time well, like the weekly timetable of Unit 4.

lessons.title: Fun: Fun with Word Games
lessons.notes_html:
Fun with Word Game — Word Search

In a Word Search puzzle, words are hidden in a grid of letters. Words can go across, down, or diagonally. In this unit's puzzle we find these 12 words:

play, collect, sing, sew, write, swim, paint, log, skip, read, mew, run

Where the Words Are Hidden

  • SKIP — row 1, columns 1–4
  • MEW — row 1, columns 8–10
  • RUN — row 2, columns 3–5
  • PAINT — column 1, rows 4–8
  • SEW — row 5, columns 8–10
  • WRITE — column 7, rows 4–8
  • SWIM — column 10, rows 4–7
  • COLLECT — row 8, columns 3–9
  • READ — row 9, columns 7–10
  • SING — row 10, columns 4–7
  • PLAY — diagonal: P (row 6, col 3) – L (row 5, col 4) – A (row 4, col 5) – Y (row 3, col 6)
  • LOG — diagonal: L (row 8, col 6) – O (row 7, col 5) – G (row 6, col 4), reading bottom-up

Funny Sentences

Read these funny sentences and make your own:

  • 'I like to collect crows.'
  • 'My sister paints all her dresses orange.'
  • 'The birds are writing with silver pencils.'
  • Model: 'My cat likes to swim and sing.'

Most of the hidden words are hobbies and actions — play, collect, sing, sew, write, swim, paint, read — which matches the unit's theme of interests, abilities and hobbies.

mcqs.q: How many words are hidden in the Word Search puzzle?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is twelve. The words are: play, collect, sing, sew, write, swim, paint, log, skip, read, mew, run. They are hidden across, down and diagonally in the letter grid.

mcqs.q: The word SKIP is found in ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: row 1, columns 1–4. The solved puzzle gives exact places: SKIP — row 1 cols 1–4; MEW — row 1 cols 8–10; RUN — row 2 cols 3–5.

mcqs.q: The word COLLECT is hidden ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: in row 8, columns 3–9. COLLECT is the longest word in the puzzle (7 letters), and it runs across row 8: C-O-L-L-E-C-T.

mcqs.q: Which word is hidden DIAGONALLY in the puzzle?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is PLAY. PLAY runs diagonally: P (row 6, col 3) – L (row 5, col 4) – A (row 4, col 5) – Y (row 3, col 6). LOG is also diagonal, reading bottom-up. The other words are across or down.

mcqs.q: The word PAINT is hidden ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: down column 1, rows 4–8. Reading top to bottom in the first column gives P-A-I-N-T. WRITE is also hidden downward, in column 7, rows 4–8.

mcqs.q: Most of the hidden words in this puzzle are ______.
options: hobbies and action words — play, sing, sew, write, swim, paint, read
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: hobbies and action words. This matches the unit's theme: 'Learning Through Personal Interests, Abilities and Hobbies'. Play, collect, sing, sew, write, swim, paint and read are all things people do as hobbies.

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of the book's funny sentences?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'I like to collect crows.' The book's funny sentences are: 'I like to collect crows', 'My sister paints all her dresses orange', and 'The birds are writing with silver pencils'. They are funny because they mix words in surprising ways.

mcqs.q: Which is a good funny sentence like the book's model?
options: 'My cat likes to swim and sing.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 'My cat likes to swim and sing.' This is the book's own model funny sentence. It is funny because cats do not swim and sing like people — mixing hobby words in strange ways makes the joke.

mcqs.q: The word MEW in the puzzle is the sound made by ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a cat. 'Mew' is the soft sound of a cat. It is hidden in row 1, columns 8–10 of the Word Search grid.

mcqs.q: In a Word Search, hidden words can run ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: across, down, or diagonally. In this puzzle, SKIP and READ run across, PAINT and WRITE run down, and PLAY and LOG run diagonally. A good player checks all directions.
